lessons.title: 1.1 Oral Communication - Boiling an Egg
lessons.notes_html:
The Dialogue

This is an oral dialogue. We practise it with a partner. Raza tells Zahid how to boil an egg, step by step.

Steps to Boil an Egg

  • Take a small pot from the cupboard.
  • Fill the pot with water.
  • Put the egg in the water carefully.
  • Put the pot on the stove.
  • The egg will be ready in about 10 minutes.

Why We Practise It

Practising this dialogue helps us learn how to give instructions and how to follow instructions in English.

Key Points

  • Raza gives the instructions and Zahid follows them.
  • The egg is put in the water carefully.
  • The egg is ready in about 10 minutes.

mcqs.q: Who tells how to boil an egg in the dialogue?
mcqs.why: In the dialogue, Raza tells Zahid the steps of boiling an egg, and Zahid follows them.

mcqs.q: What does Zahid take first?
mcqs.why: Raza first tells Zahid to take a small pot from the cupboard.

mcqs.q: Where is the pot kept?
mcqs.why: Raza tells Zahid to take a small pot from the cupboard.

mcqs.q: What is filled in the pot?
mcqs.why: After taking the pot, Zahid fills it with water and puts the egg in it.

mcqs.q: How should the egg be put in the water?
mcqs.why: Raza says to put the egg in the water carefully, so that it does not break.

mcqs.q: Where is the pot put after adding the egg?
mcqs.why: The pot is put on the stove so that the water boils and the egg cooks.

mcqs.q: In how much time will the egg be ready?
mcqs.why: Raza tells Zahid that the egg will be ready in about 10 minutes.

mcqs.q: What do we learn from practising this dialogue?
options: How to give and follow instructions
mcqs.why: Practising this dialogue helps us learn how to lead and follow instructions in English.

mcqs.q: What is put in the water to boil?
mcqs.why: The dialogue is about boiling an egg, so an egg is put in the water.

mcqs.q: Who follows the instructions in the dialogue?
mcqs.why: Zahid listens to Raza and follows each step to boil the egg.

lessons.title: 1.2 Reading - Sara Falls Sick
lessons.notes_html:
The Story

Sana and Sara are best friends. They play together in the evening. One day Sara fell sick. She had fever and an upset stomach. Sana went to see her.

Who Said These Words?

  • "What happened?" - Sana said this.
  • "I am not feeling well." - Sara said this.
  • "The doctor said you must wash your hands before eating." - Sara's mother said this.
  • "You are my best friend." - Sara said this to Sana.

Good Habits

  • We must brush our teeth every day, in the morning and before going to bed.
  • We must wash our hands before eating.
  • We must clip our nails once a week.
  • Germs make us fall sick. They get into our stomach with our food when our hands, nails and teeth are not clean.
  • We take medicines when we have fever or stomach ache.

Key Points

  • Sara had fever and an upset stomach.
  • Washing hands before eating is a healthy habit.
  • Germs make us fall sick.

mcqs.q: Who fell sick in the story?
mcqs.why: Sara fell sick. She had fever and an upset stomach, and Sana went to see her.

mcqs.q: Who is Sara's best friend?
mcqs.why: Sana and Sara are best friends. Sara herself says, "You are my best friend."

mcqs.q: When do Sana and Sara play together?
mcqs.why: The story says the two friends play together in the evening, not in the morning.

mcqs.q: What happened to Sara?
options: She had fever and an upset stomach
mcqs.why: Sara had high fever and stomach upset, so her mother gave her medicine.

mcqs.q: Who said, "What happened?"
mcqs.why: When Sana came to see her sick friend, she asked Sara, "What happened?"

mcqs.q: What did the doctor say we must do?
mcqs.why: Sara's mother said the doctor had told them to wash their hands before eating.

mcqs.q: When must we brush our teeth?
options: In the morning and before going to bed
mcqs.why: We must brush our teeth every day, in the morning and before going to bed.

mcqs.q: How often must we clip our nails?
mcqs.why: The lesson says we must clip our nails once a week, not every day.

mcqs.q: What makes us fall sick?
mcqs.why: Germs make us fall sick. That is why we keep our hands, nails and teeth clean.

mcqs.q: How do germs get into our stomach?
options: With our food when our hands are not clean
mcqs.why: Germs get into our stomach with our food when our hands, nails and teeth are not clean.

lessons.title: 1.3 Writing - Making a Fruit Salad
lessons.notes_html:
Words and Pictures

In this lesson we match action words with pictures: peel an orange, cut the apples, add the grapes and peel and cut a mango.

Steps of Making a Fruit Salad

  • Step 1: First, take a bowl.
  • Step 2: Next, peel and cut an orange.
  • Step 3: Then, peel and cut a mango.
  • Step 4: After that, cut the apples.
  • Step 5: Finally, add the grapes.
  • Step 6: Yummy fruit salad is ready.

The steps must be in the right order, or the salad will not be made properly. The order words are First, Next, Then, After that and Finally.

A Recipe Card

A recipe card shows the name of the dish, its ingredients and tools, and the steps. Example: a vegetable sandwich needs bread slices, cucumber, tomato, cheese, butter, a knife and a plate. First put butter on the bread, then cucumber and tomato, then cheese, cover it and cut it.

Key Points

  • First take a bowl, then peel and cut the fruits.
  • Grapes are added finally.
  • A recipe card has a name, ingredients, tools and steps.

mcqs.q: What do we take first to make a fruit salad?
mcqs.why: Step 1 of making a fruit salad is: First, take a bowl.

mcqs.q: Which fruit is peeled and cut in Step 2?
mcqs.why: Step 2 says: Next, peel and cut an orange. The mango comes in Step 3.

mcqs.q: What do we do after peeling and cutting the mango?
mcqs.why: Step 4 says: After that, cut the apples. The grapes are added finally, in Step 5.

mcqs.q: When are the grapes added?
mcqs.why: Step 5 says: Finally, add the grapes. Then the yummy fruit salad is ready.

mcqs.q: Which words show the order of steps?
options: First, Next, Then, After that, Finally
mcqs.why: First, Next, Then, After that and Finally are the order words used for the steps.

mcqs.q: What does a recipe card show?
options: Only the name of the dish
The name, ingredients, tools and steps of a dish
mcqs.why: A recipe card shows the name of the dish, its ingredients and tools, and the steps to make it.

mcqs.q: In the vegetable sandwich recipe, what is put on the bread first?
mcqs.why: Step 1 of the sandwich recipe is: Put butter on the bread slices.

mcqs.q: Which of these is a tool in the sandwich recipe?
mcqs.why: The tools listed for the vegetable sandwich are a knife and a plate.

mcqs.q: Why must the steps of a recipe be in the right order?
options: To make the dish look big
Or the dish will not be made properly
mcqs.why: The lesson says the steps must be in the right order, or the salad will not be made properly.

mcqs.q: What do we do with the apples in a fruit salad?
mcqs.why: In Step 4 we cut the apples and put them in the bowl with the other fruits.

lessons.title: 1.3 Writing - Punctuation Marks
lessons.notes_html:
Punctuation Rules

  • Names and the first word of a sentence begin with a capital letter.
  • Items in a list are separated by commas.
  • A statement ends with a full stop.
  • A question ends with a question mark.

Correct Sentences

  • Ali, Rehan, Faisal and Sadia were friends.
  • They enjoyed reading, colouring, eating mangoes, climbing trees and playing in the corn fields.
  • They had fun in school.
  • Do you like your school?
  • What is your friend's name?

Key Points

  • Capital letters are used for names and sentence beginnings.
  • Commas separate items in a list.
  • Questions end with a question mark.

mcqs.q: Which sentence is written correctly?
options: ali rehan faisal and sadia were friends
Ali, Rehan, Faisal and Sadia were friends.
Ali Rehan Faisal and Sadia were friends
ali, rehan, faisal and sadia were friends.
mcqs.why: Names begin with capital letters, commas separate the names in the list, and the sentence ends with a full stop.

mcqs.q: A question ends with a:
mcqs.why: Questions end with a question mark, like "Do you like your school?"

mcqs.q: Names begin with:
mcqs.why: Names of people and places begin with capital letters, like Ali and Sadia.

mcqs.q: Items in a list are separated by:
mcqs.why: Commas separate items in a list, as in "reading, colouring, eating mangoes".

mcqs.q: A statement ends with a:
mcqs.why: A statement, like "They had fun in school." ends with a full stop.

mcqs.q: Which one is a question?
mcqs.why: "What is your friend's name?" asks something and ends with a question mark, so it is a question.

mcqs.q: What is the correct form of "what is your name"?
mcqs.why: A question begins with a capital letter and ends with a question mark.

mcqs.q: In "They enjoyed reading, colouring and playing", the commas separate:
mcqs.why: The commas separate the activities in the list: reading, colouring and playing.

mcqs.q: Which word needs a capital letter in "ali is my friend"?
mcqs.why: Ali is a name, and names always begin with a capital letter.

mcqs.q: How many commas are there in "Ali, Rehan, Faisal and Sadia were friends"?
mcqs.why: There are three commas: after Ali, after Rehan and after Faisal.

lessons.title: 1.3 Poem - Healthy Food
lessons.notes_html:
The Poem

The poem "Healthy Food" names many foods: fruits, vegetables, meat, rice, sugar, corn, wheat, chicken, mutton, beef, fish, eggs, nuts, beans, apples, bananas, grapes, mango, carrots, onions, peas and potato.

Why Healthy Food?

Healthy foods give us strength, protect us from getting ill and save us from taking pills.

Our Meals

  • Breakfast: a boiled egg with bread, and tea or warm milk with bread, jam and butter.
  • Lunch: rice, chicken and vegetables. In winter, a hot cup of soup after it.
  • Dinner: meat, potato and salad.

Eating a healthy lunch keeps us active for the rest of the day.

Key Points

  • The poem names fruits, vegetables, meat, eggs and many other foods.
  • Healthy food gives us strength and keeps us safe from illness.
  • Breakfast, lunch and dinner should all be healthy.

mcqs.q: Which food is named in the poem "Healthy Food"?
mcqs.why: The poem names mango among its fruits, along with apples, bananas and grapes. Pizza, burger and chips are not in the poem.

mcqs.q: Healthy food gives us:
mcqs.why: The lesson says healthy foods give us strength and protect us from getting ill.

mcqs.q: Healthy food protects us from:
mcqs.why: Healthy foods protect us from getting ill and save us from taking pills.

mcqs.q: Which of these is a vegetable named in the poem?
mcqs.why: Carrots are a vegetable. Banana, grapes and apple are fruits named in the poem.

mcqs.q: What is eaten for breakfast in the book's example?
mcqs.why: The book gives breakfast as the example: a boiled egg with bread, and tea or warm milk.

mcqs.q: What is served with bread at breakfast in the example?
mcqs.why: The example breakfast is tea or warm milk with bread, jam and butter.

mcqs.q: What is eaten for lunch in the example answer?
mcqs.why: The lunch answer is rice, chicken and vegetables, with a hot cup of soup in winter.

mcqs.q: What is eaten for dinner in the example answer?
mcqs.why: The dinner answer is meat, potato and salad.

mcqs.q: In winter, what does the writer drink after lunch?
mcqs.why: The paragraph says: In winter, I drink a hot cup of soup after lunch.

mcqs.q: Eating a healthy lunch keeps us:
options: Active for the rest of the day
mcqs.why: The lesson says eating a healthy lunch keeps me active for the rest of the day.

lessons.title: 1.4 Grammar - Proper and Common Nouns
lessons.notes_html:
Two Kinds of Nouns

A proper noun is the special name of a particular person or place. It is written with a capital letter. A common noun is a general name for people, places, animals and things.

From the Text "Friends"

  • Shiharu - girl - from Japan
  • Sarah - girl - from Turkey
  • Tokyo - city
  • Istanbul - city
  • Iqbal - boy
  • Tahir - boy

Proper nouns: Shiharu, Japan, Sarah, Turkey, Tokyo, Istanbul, Iqbal, Tahir. Common nouns: girl, boy, city, country.

Key Points

  • Proper nouns are special names and begin with capital letters.
  • Common nouns are general names: girl, boy, city, country.
  • Japan and Turkey are countries; Tokyo and Istanbul are cities.

mcqs.q: Which one is a proper noun?
mcqs.why: Tokyo is the special name of one city, so it is a proper noun and begins with a capital letter.

mcqs.q: Which one is a common noun?
mcqs.why: City is a general name for all cities, so it is a common noun. Japan, Sarah and Istanbul are proper nouns.

mcqs.q: Shiharu is a girl from:
mcqs.why: In the text "Friends", Shiharu is a girl and Japan is her country.

mcqs.q: Sarah is from:
mcqs.why: In the text, Sarah is a girl from Turkey. Tokyo and Istanbul are cities.

mcqs.q: Tokyo is a:
mcqs.why: Tokyo is a city. Its proper noun is Tokyo and its common noun is city.

mcqs.q: The common noun for Istanbul is:
mcqs.why: Istanbul is the proper noun and city is its common noun.

mcqs.q: Iqbal and Tahir are:
mcqs.why: Iqbal and Tahir are boys, so their common noun is boy.

mcqs.q: Proper nouns are written with:
mcqs.why: Proper nouns name a particular person or place and are written with a capital letter.

mcqs.q: The common noun for Japan is:
mcqs.why: Japan is the proper noun for a country, so its common noun is country.

mcqs.q: Which pair is correct?
mcqs.why: Sarah is a girl. Shiharu is also a girl, Tokyo is a city, and Sarah is not a boy.

lessons.title: 1.4 Grammar - Pronouns
lessons.notes_html:
What is a Pronoun?

A pronoun is a word used in place of a noun. We use we for the speaker and others, she for a girl or woman, he for a boy or man, it for a thing, and they for more than one person.

Matching Pronouns

  • Pasha and I - we
  • Jamila - she
  • Fakhir - he
  • The big truck - it
  • Khadija and Maryam - they

Replacing Words with Pronouns

  • Jamil - He; Jamil and Kamal - They; Jasmeen - She
  • Sonia - Her; the match - It; Fareed and I - We
  • Jamil's parents - Them; me and my sister - Us; Samad - Him

Key Points

  • A pronoun is used in place of a noun.
  • He is for a boy or man; she is for a girl or woman.
  • It is for a thing; they is for more than one person.

mcqs.q: Which pronoun can replace "Pasha and I"?
mcqs.why: "Pasha and I" includes the speaker, so the pronoun is "we".

mcqs.q: Which pronoun can replace "Jamila"?
mcqs.why: Jamila is a girl, so the pronoun for her is "she".

mcqs.q: Which pronoun can replace "the big truck"?
mcqs.why: A truck is a thing, and the pronoun for a thing is "it".

mcqs.q: Which pronoun can replace "Khadija and Maryam"?
mcqs.why: Khadija and Maryam are two people, so the pronoun is "they".

mcqs.q: Jamil likes reading books. ___ likes reading books.
mcqs.why: Jamil is a boy, so we use "he" in place of his name.

mcqs.q: Humaira will go to the shop with Sonia. She will go with ___.
mcqs.why: Sonia is a girl, and here the pronoun comes after "with", so we use "her".

mcqs.q: Fareed will go with Jamil's parents. He will go with ___.
mcqs.why: Jamil's parents are more than one person, so the pronoun is "them".

mcqs.q: "Please give me and my sister some food!" Give ___ some food.
mcqs.why: "Me and my sister" includes the speaker, so the pronoun is "us".

mcqs.q: The teacher gave Samad good marks. The teacher gave ___ good marks.
mcqs.why: Samad is a boy, so the pronoun used for him here is "him".

mcqs.q: A pronoun is a word used:
mcqs.why: Pronouns are words used in place of nouns, like he, she, it, we and they.

lessons.title: 1.4 Grammar - Linking Words
lessons.notes_html:
Four Linking Words

  • but - shows contrast (a different idea)
  • because - shows a reason
  • and - joins or adds things
  • so - shows a result

Saifullah the Old Man

Saifullah was an old man but he had lots of energy. He was healthy because he always ate healthy food and washed his hands. He loved eating chicken and bread. One day he was sick so he did not go to the fields. He sent his son Arif to plough the land.

Sentences about Ourselves

  • I do not like peaches but I like mangoes.
  • My mother loves me because I help her at home.
  • Yesterday I did my homework so my teacher praised me.

Key Points

  • But is for contrast, because is for reason.
  • And joins things, so shows a result.
  • Linking words join two ideas in one sentence.

mcqs.q: The linking word "but" shows:
mcqs.why: "But" shows contrast, as in "Saifullah was an old man but he had lots of energy."

mcqs.q: The linking word "because" shows:
mcqs.why: "Because" gives the reason, as in "He was healthy because he always ate healthy food."

mcqs.q: The linking word "so" shows:
mcqs.why: "So" shows a result, as in "He was sick so he did not go to the fields."

mcqs.q: Saifullah was an old man ___ he had lots of energy.
mcqs.why: Being old and having lots of energy are opposite ideas, so we use "but" for contrast.

mcqs.q: He was healthy ___ he always ate healthy food and washed his hands.
mcqs.why: Eating healthy food is the reason he was healthy, so we use "because".

mcqs.q: He loved eating chicken ___ bread.
mcqs.why: "And" joins the two foods he loved eating: chicken and bread.

mcqs.q: One day he was sick ___ he did not go to the fields.
mcqs.why: Not going to the fields was the result of being sick, so we use "so".

mcqs.q: Who did Saifullah send to plough the land?
mcqs.why: When Saifullah was sick, he sent his son Arif to plough the land.

mcqs.q: I do not like peaches ___ I like mangoes.
mcqs.why: Not liking peaches and liking mangoes are contrasting ideas, so we use "but".

mcqs.q: Yesterday I did my homework ___ my teacher praised me.
mcqs.why: The teacher praising me was the result of doing my homework, so we use "so".

lessons.title: 1.5 Study Skills - Food Words and Colours
lessons.notes_html:
Related Words for "Food"

When we hear the word food, these words come to mind: rice, bread, milk, egg, apple, banana, chicken. Learning related words together helps us learn new vocabulary in groups.

Food Items by Colour

  • Red: tomato, beetroot, pomegranate, cherries, plums, strawberries
  • Green: spinach, okra, capsicum, apples, grapes, pistachio
  • Brown: wheat, potato, sweet potato, ginger, almonds, dried dates
  • Yellow: banana, pineapple, daal moong, cheese, butter, mango, papaya

Key Points

  • Related words are learned together in groups.
  • Tomato and cherries are red; spinach and okra are green.
  • Banana, mango and cheese are yellow; almonds and dates are brown.

mcqs.q: Which of these is a red food?
mcqs.why: Tomato is in the red list, with beetroot, pomegranate, cherries, plums and strawberries.

mcqs.q: Which of these is a green food?
mcqs.why: Spinach is in the green list, with okra, capsicum, apples, grapes and pistachio.

mcqs.q: Which of these is a yellow food?
mcqs.why: Banana is in the yellow list, with pineapple, cheese, butter, mango and papaya.

mcqs.q: Which of these is a brown food?
mcqs.why: Potato is in the brown list, with wheat, sweet potato, ginger, almonds and dried dates.

mcqs.q: Learning related words together helps us to:
mcqs.why: Thinking of related words together helps us learn new vocabulary in groups.

mcqs.q: Which of these is a food word?
mcqs.why: Chicken is a food item. Pencil, chair and bus are not foods.

mcqs.q: Pomegranate is in which colour list?
mcqs.why: Pomegranate is listed with the red foods: tomato, beetroot, cherries, plums and strawberries.

mcqs.q: Pistachio is in which colour list?
mcqs.why: Pistachio is in the green list, with spinach, okra, capsicum, apples and grapes.

mcqs.q: Cheese and butter are in which colour list?
mcqs.why: Cheese and butter are yellow foods, like banana, pineapple, mango and papaya.

mcqs.q: Almonds and dried dates are in which colour list?
mcqs.why: Almonds and dried dates are in the brown list, with wheat, potato and ginger.

lessons.title: 1.6 Fun - Hand Wash Role Play
lessons.notes_html:
The Role Play

This is a fun activity. Some children act as the germs, one child is the hand and one is the soap.

What They Say

  • The germs say: "I will make you sick," and attack the hand.
  • The hand says: "I want soap to wash my hands."
  • The soap says: "Use me to kill the germs."

What It Teaches Us

Washing hands with soap kills germs and keeps us safe from sickness.

Key Points

  • The germs try to make the hand sick.
  • The hand asks for soap.
  • Soap kills the germs and keeps us safe.

mcqs.q: Who says, "I will make you sick"?
mcqs.why: In the role play, the germs say, "I will make you sick," and attack the hand.

mcqs.q: What does the hand want in the role play?
mcqs.why: The hand says, "I want soap to wash my hands."

mcqs.q: What does the soap say?
mcqs.why: The soap says, "Use me to kill the germs," because soap kills germs.

mcqs.q: Washing hands with soap:
mcqs.why: This fun activity teaches us that washing hands with soap kills germs.

mcqs.q: This role play teaches us to:
mcqs.why: The role play teaches that washing hands with soap keeps us safe from sickness.

mcqs.q: Germs can make us:
mcqs.why: The germs say, "I will make you sick," because germs make us fall sick.

mcqs.q: Who attacks the hand in the play?
mcqs.why: The germs attack the hand and try to make it sick.

mcqs.q: To stay safe from sickness, we must:
mcqs.why: Washing hands with soap kills germs and keeps us safe from sickness.

mcqs.q: From Unit 1, when must we wash our hands?
mcqs.why: The doctor said we must wash our hands before eating, as we learned in "Sara Falls Sick".

mcqs.q: The soap helps the hand by:
mcqs.why: The soap says, "Use me to kill the germs," so it helps the hand by killing the germs.

lessons.title: 2.1 Oral Communication - Visiting a Friend
lessons.notes_html:
The Dialogue

This is an oral dialogue between two friends, Ahmed and Bilal. We practise it with a partner.

What Happens

  • Ahmed tells Bilal that he was waiting for him yesterday.
  • Bilal says sorry because he could not come due to some work.
  • Bilal asks if they can go outside to play.
  • Ahmed's mother is not home, so he has to stay at home.
  • They decide to play ludo inside the house.

Why We Practise It

Practising this dialogue teaches us polite expressions and how to exchange social courtesies, like saying sorry.

Key Points

  • Bilal could not come yesterday because of some work.
  • Ahmed cannot go out because his mother is not home.
  • The two friends play ludo inside.

mcqs.q: Who was waiting for his friend yesterday?
mcqs.why: Ahmed tells Bilal that he was waiting for him yesterday.

mcqs.q: Why could Bilal not come yesterday?
mcqs.why: Bilal says sorry because he could not come due to some work.

mcqs.q: What does Bilal say when he comes?
mcqs.why: Bilal says sorry because he could not come the day before. Saying sorry is a polite expression.

mcqs.q: What does Bilal ask Ahmed?
options: If they can go outside to play
If he can borrow a book
If he can stay at night
mcqs.why: Bilal asks Ahmed if they can go outside to play.

mcqs.q: Why does Ahmed have to stay at home?
mcqs.why: Ahmed's mother is not home, so he has to stay at home and cannot go outside.

mcqs.q: What do the two friends decide to play inside?
mcqs.why: They decide to play ludo inside the house because Ahmed cannot go out.

mcqs.q: This dialogue teaches us:
mcqs.why: Practising this dialogue teaches us polite expressions and how to exchange social courtesies.

mcqs.q: Who comes to visit his friend in the dialogue?
mcqs.why: Bilal is the friend who comes to visit Ahmed at his home.

mcqs.q: Where do the friends play ludo?
mcqs.why: They play ludo inside the house because Ahmed has to stay at home.

mcqs.q: Ahmed was waiting for Bilal:
mcqs.why: Ahmed says he was waiting for Bilal yesterday, but Bilal could not come.

lessons.title: 2.2 Reading - Stay Safe
lessons.notes_html:
The Text

The text "Stay Safe" tells us the safety rules that Maryam follows. In the text, the word always comes 5 times, parents comes 7 times and do not comes 6 times.

Word Meanings

  • obey - follow
  • take - accept
  • easily seen - prominent
  • anything that can hurt - harmful
  • shout loudly - yell
  • a person we do not know - stranger

Maryam's Safety Rules

  • She knows her parents' names, their telephone numbers and her address.
  • She takes permission before she goes anywhere.
  • She checks first with her parents before she accepts anything from others.
  • She takes a friend with her when she goes to play outside.
  • If someone scares her, she says no, gets away and shouts for help.
  • She always tells everything to her parents.

Key Points

  • Every child should know their parents' names, phone numbers and address.
  • We should not open the door for or talk to a stranger.
  • We should always obey our parents.

mcqs.q: How many times does the word "parents" come in the text "Stay Safe"?
mcqs.why: In the text, "always" comes 5 times, "parents" comes 7 times and "do not" comes 6 times.

mcqs.q: What is the meaning of "obey"?
mcqs.why: In the text, "obey" means follow, as in obeying our parents.

mcqs.q: A person we do not know is called a:
mcqs.why: A person we do not know is called a stranger. We should not talk to a stranger.

mcqs.q: What is the meaning of "prominent"?
mcqs.why: "Prominent" means easily seen. We should put important phone numbers in a prominent place.

mcqs.q: Maryam knows her parents' names, their telephone numbers and her:
mcqs.why: Maryam knows her parents' names, their telephone numbers and her address.

mcqs.q: What does Maryam do before she goes anywhere?
mcqs.why: Maryam takes permission from her parents before she goes anywhere.

mcqs.q: What does Maryam do before accepting anything from others?
options: She checks first with her parents
mcqs.why: She checks first with her parents before she accepts anything from others.

mcqs.q: Who does Maryam take with her when she goes to play outside?
mcqs.why: Maryam takes a friend with her when she goes to play outside.

mcqs.q: If someone scares Maryam, what does she do?
options: She says no, gets away and shouts for help
mcqs.why: Maryam says no, gets away and shouts for help, and she tells everything to her parents.

mcqs.q: Which of these is a safety rule?
options: Open the door for a stranger
mcqs.why: We should obey our parents. We should not open the door for a stranger or play with sharp things.

lessons.title: 2.3 Writing - Poem: Crossing the Road
lessons.notes_html:
Rhyming Words

Rhyming words sound the same at the end. In the poem "Crossing the Road", the rhyming pairs are:

  • see - me (more: bee, knee)
  • well - bell (more: sell, tell)
  • bit - hit (more: sit, fit)
  • clear - near (more: dear, fear)
  • wide - side (more: ride, tide)

A Small Rhyming Poem

I see a tiny bee. It did not bite me. I ran and hurt my knee. A good poem uses rhyming words at the ends of lines and paints a small picture in words.

Key Points

  • Rhyming words have the same ending sound.
  • See rhymes with me; well rhymes with bell.
  • We can add new words to a rhyming family.

mcqs.q: Which word rhymes with "see" in the poem?
mcqs.why: In the poem "Crossing the Road", see rhymes with me. Bee and knee also rhyme with them.

mcqs.q: Which word rhymes with "well"?
mcqs.why: Well rhymes with bell. Sell and tell are more words in the same family.

mcqs.q: Which pair rhymes?
mcqs.why: Bit rhymes with hit. Sit and fit also belong to this rhyming family.

mcqs.q: Which words can be added to the family of "clear - near"?
mcqs.why: Dear and fear end with the same sound as clear and near, so they join that family.

mcqs.q: Which words can be added to the family of "wide - side"?
mcqs.why: Ride and tide rhyme with wide and side because they end with the same sound.

mcqs.q: Rhyming words are words that:
options: Sound the same at the end
mcqs.why: Rhyming words sound the same at the end, like see and me or well and bell.

mcqs.q: In the small poem, what did the child see?
mcqs.why: The small poem begins: I see a tiny bee. It did not bite me.

mcqs.q: What did the child hurt in the small poem?
mcqs.why: The poem says: I ran and hurt my knee. Knee rhymes with bee and me.

mcqs.q: A good poem uses rhyming words:
mcqs.why: A good poem uses rhyming words at the ends of lines and paints a small picture in words.

mcqs.q: Which word rhymes with "bell"?
mcqs.why: Tell rhymes with bell and well. All three end with the same sound.

lessons.title: 2.3 Writing - Sentences in Order
lessons.notes_html:
Amina Clears the Table

Sentences must be in the right order to tell what really happened:

  • First, Amina cleared the table.
  • Then, she put the plates, bowls and spoons in the kitchen.
  • Next, she washed them with hot water and dish washing soap.
  • After that, she dried them with the towel.
  • Finally, she arranged all the things on the shelf.

My Day in Class

We use first, next, then, after that and finally to show the order of our day: First I reached my class, next I opened my English book, then I wrote the new words, after that I answered the teacher's questions, and finally I packed my bag and went home.

Key Points

  • Order words show the order in which things happen.
  • First comes at the beginning and finally at the end.
  • Sentences in order tell the story step by step.

mcqs.q: What did Amina do first?
mcqs.why: First, Amina cleared the table. Only then did she take the dishes to the kitchen.

mcqs.q: What did Amina do after clearing the table?
options: She put the plates, bowls and spoons in the kitchen
She dried them with a towel
She arranged them on the shelf
mcqs.why: Then she put the plates, bowls and spoons in the kitchen, before washing them.

mcqs.q: With what did Amina wash the dishes?
options: Hot water and dish washing soap
mcqs.why: Next, she washed them with hot water and dish washing soap.

mcqs.q: What did Amina do after washing the dishes?
options: She dried them with the towel
mcqs.why: After that, she dried them with the towel, and finally arranged them on the shelf.

mcqs.q: What did Amina do finally?
options: She arranged all the things on the shelf
mcqs.why: Finally, she arranged all the things on the shelf. Finally shows the last step.

mcqs.q: Which word shows the last step?
mcqs.why: "Finally" shows the last step. "First" shows the first step of the order.

mcqs.q: In the class-day sentences, what did the child do first?
options: Reached the class and said good morning to the teacher
mcqs.why: First, I reached my class and said good morning to my teacher.

mcqs.q: What did the child do after opening the English book and reading?
options: Wrote the new words in the notebook
mcqs.why: Then, I wrote the new words in my notebook, after reading the lesson.

mcqs.q: What did the child do finally in class?
options: Packed the bag and went home happily
mcqs.why: Finally, I packed my bag and went home happily. It is the last step of the day.

mcqs.q: Order words like first, next and finally show:
mcqs.why: Using first, next, then, after that and finally shows the order of our day clearly.

lessons.title: 2.4 Grammar - Action Verbs
lessons.notes_html:
What is a Verb?

Verbs are action words. They tell us what people, animals and things do.

Action Verbs

  • open - to move something so it is no longer closed, like opening a door
  • rest - to relax and take a break
  • eat - to take food into the mouth
  • fly - to move through the air, like a bird
  • drink - to take water or milk into the mouth
  • kick - to hit something with the foot, like kicking a ball

Verbs in the Do's and Don'ts

Do's: put, obey, remove, stay, scream, go. Don'ts: play, open, point, stand, listen. Verbs are used everywhere: in rules, stories and instructions.

Sentences with Verbs

  • I open my book to read the lesson.
  • Birds fly high in the sky.
  • Ali can kick the ball very far.

Key Points

  • A verb is an action word.
  • Eat, drink, fly, kick, open and rest are action verbs.
  • Every sentence has a main verb that tells what the subject does.

mcqs.q: What is a verb?
mcqs.why: Verbs are action words. They tell us what people, animals and things do.

mcqs.q: What does the verb "kick" mean?
options: To hit something with the foot
To take food into the mouth
To relax and take a break
mcqs.why: Kick means to hit something with the foot, like kicking a ball.

mcqs.q: What does the verb "fly" mean?
mcqs.why: Fly means to move through the air, like a bird.

mcqs.q: Which sentence uses the verb "drink" correctly?
options: I drink a glass of milk every morning.
mcqs.why: Drink means to take water or milk into the mouth, so we drink a glass of milk.

mcqs.q: Which verb is in the list of Do's?
mcqs.why: The Do's verbs are put, obey, remove, stay, scream and go. Obey is one of them.

mcqs.q: Which verb is in the list of Don'ts?
mcqs.why: The Don'ts verbs are play, open, point, stand and listen. Play is one of them.

mcqs.q: "After playing, I rest for a while." The verb "rest" means:
options: To relax and take a break
mcqs.why: Rest means to relax and take a break, which we do after playing.

mcqs.q: Which word is an action verb?
mcqs.why: Eat is an action verb: to take food into the mouth. Book, happy and big are not actions.

mcqs.q: "I open my book to read the lesson." What does "open" mean here?
options: To move something so it is no longer closed
mcqs.why: Open means to move something so it is no longer closed, like opening a door or a book.

mcqs.q: Verbs are used everywhere in:
mcqs.why: Finding verbs in a real text shows us that verbs are used everywhere, in rules, stories and instructions.

lessons.title: 2.4 Grammar - The Verb Be
lessons.notes_html:
Am, Is, Are

The verb "be" has three forms: am with I, is with one person or thing, and are with more than one.

  • I am a student. He is my brother. They are brothers.
  • My cat is drinking milk. The teachers are looking at the paintings.

Main Verb or Helping Verb?

In "I am a student", am is the main verb. In "She is sleeping", is is a helping verb because it helps the main verb "sleeping". A helping verb comes with a verb ending in -ing.

The Eid Milan Party

We are planning a party. I am cleaning my class. One of my friends is making an invitation card. Our teacher is helping us.

Key Points

  • Am is used with I; is with one; are with more than one.
  • Be can be a main verb or a helping verb.
  • As a helping verb, be comes with an -ing verb.

mcqs.q: Jamila and Azra ___ good friends.
mcqs.why: Jamila and Azra are two people, so we use "are" with more than one.

mcqs.q: My cat ___ drinking milk.
mcqs.why: The cat is one animal, so we use "is": My cat is drinking milk.

mcqs.q: I ___ tired, so I ___ going to sleep.
mcqs.why: We always use "am" with I: I am tired, so I am going to sleep.

mcqs.q: The teachers ___ looking at the paintings.
mcqs.why: The teachers are more than one person, so we use "are".

mcqs.q: She ___ a cute baby.
mcqs.why: She is one person, so we use "is": She is a cute baby.

mcqs.q: In "She is sleeping", the word "is" is:
mcqs.why: In "She is sleeping", "is" is a helping verb because it helps the main verb "sleeping".

mcqs.q: In "I am a student", the word "am" is:
mcqs.why: In "I am a student", there is no other verb, so "am" is the main verb.

mcqs.q: We ___ planning to have an Eid Milan party.
mcqs.why: We is more than one person, so we use "are": We are planning.

mcqs.q: One of my friends ___ making an invitation card.
mcqs.why: One friend is a single person, so we use "is": One of my friends is making a card.

mcqs.q: There ___ many students in my class.
mcqs.why: Many students means more than one, so we say: There are many students in my class.

lessons.title: 2.5 Study Skills - School and Home Words
lessons.notes_html:
Related Words

  • School: teacher, book, classroom, student, bag, pencil, bell
  • Home: mother, father, bed, kitchen, garden, family, dinner

Grouping related words together helps us remember vocabulary and use it when we speak and write.

Alphabetical Order

Alphabetical order means arranging words by their first letters, from A to Z. It is the order used in dictionaries.

Bag, bell, book, classroom, dinner, family, father, garden, kitchen, mother, pencil, student, teacher.

Key Points

  • School words: teacher, book, classroom, student, bag, pencil, bell.
  • Home words: mother, father, bed, kitchen, garden, family, dinner.
  • Dictionaries arrange words in alphabetical order.

mcqs.q: Which word is related to "School"?
mcqs.why: Classroom is a school word, with teacher, book, student, bag, pencil and bell.

mcqs.q: Which word is related to "Home"?
mcqs.why: Kitchen is a home word, with mother, father, bed, garden, family and dinner.

mcqs.q: Alphabetical order means arranging words:
options: By their first letters, from A to Z
mcqs.why: Alphabetical order means arranging words by their first letters, from A to Z.

mcqs.q: Which word comes first in alphabetical order?
mcqs.why: Bag, bell and book all start with B, but "ba" comes before "be", so bag comes first.

mcqs.q: Which is the correct alphabetical order?
mcqs.why: Bag comes before bell (ba before be), and bell comes before book (be before bo).

mcqs.q: Dictionaries arrange words in:
mcqs.why: Alphabetical order is the order used in dictionaries, so we can find words easily.

mcqs.q: Which word comes last in alphabetical order: teacher, book, pencil, bell?
mcqs.why: T comes after B and P in the alphabet, so teacher comes last.

mcqs.q: Grouping related words together helps us to:
mcqs.why: Grouping related words together helps us remember vocabulary and use it in speaking and writing.

mcqs.q: Which of these is a home word?
mcqs.why: Dinner is a home word. Student, bell and classroom are school words.

mcqs.q: In alphabetical order, which comes first: family or father?
mcqs.why: Both start with "fa", but the third letter of family is "m" and of father is "t"; m comes before t, so family comes first.

lessons.title: 2.6 Fun - Word Chain and Odd Word Out
lessons.notes_html:
Word Chain Game

In a word chain, each new word begins with the last letter of the word before it.

LOOK ends with K, so KEEP follows. KEEP ends with P, so PRAY follows. PRAY ends with Y, so we can add YELLOW. YELLOW ends with W, so we add WATCH. WATCH ends with H, so we add HAPPY.

Odd Word Out

  • boy, female, woman, girl - the odd one is boy, because the others are all females.
  • shoe, sandal, socks, boot - the odd one is socks, because the others are kinds of shoes worn outside; socks are worn inside shoes.
  • lake, forest, ocean, river - the odd one is forest, because the others are bodies of water.
  • chair, seat, table, sofa - the odd one is table, because the others are things we sit on.
  • rice, fish, chicken, beef - the odd one is rice, because the others are kinds of meat.

Key Points

  • In a word chain, the next word starts with the last letter of the previous word.
  • In Odd Word Out, we find the word that does not belong to the group.
  • We must also give a reason for our choice.

mcqs.q: In a word chain, each new word begins with:
options: The first letter of the word before it
The last letter of the word before it
mcqs.why: Each new word must begin with the last letter of the word written before it.

mcqs.q: LOOK ends with K. Which word can follow it?
mcqs.why: LOOK ends with K, so a word beginning with K follows it: KEEP.

mcqs.q: After PRAY, which word can come next in the chain?
mcqs.why: PRAY ends with Y, so YELLOW follows it in the chain given in the book.

mcqs.q: WATCH ends with H. Which word follows it in the chain?
mcqs.why: WATCH ends with H, so HAPPY, which begins with H, follows it.

mcqs.q: Odd one out: boy, female, woman, girl.
mcqs.why: Boy is the odd one out because female, woman and girl are all females.

mcqs.q: Odd one out: shoe, sandal, socks, boot.
mcqs.why: Socks are worn inside shoes, while shoe, sandal and boot are kinds of shoes worn on the feet outside.

mcqs.q: Odd one out: lake, forest, ocean, river.
mcqs.why: Forest is the odd one out because lake, ocean and river are all bodies of water.

mcqs.q: Odd one out: chair, seat, table, sofa.
mcqs.why: Table is the odd one out because chair, seat and sofa are all things we sit on.

mcqs.q: Odd one out: rice, fish, chicken, beef.
mcqs.why: Rice is the odd one out because fish, chicken and beef are all kinds of meat.

mcqs.q: In the Odd Word Out game, we must also:
mcqs.why: We circle the word that is different and write our reason for choosing it.

lessons.title: 3.1 Oral Communication - Winning a Prize
lessons.notes_html:
The Dialogue

This is an oral dialogue between Hakeem and Ahmed. We practise it with a partner.

What Happens

  • Hakeem happily tells Ahmed that he won an essay competition.
  • He will get a new bicycle as the first prize in about a week.
  • Ahmed asks if Hakeem will give him a ride.
  • Hakeem says sure, because he will not enjoy his gift if he does not share it with his friend.

Why We Practise It

Practising this dialogue teaches us how to express joy and share happiness with friends.

Key Points

  • Hakeem won the first prize in an essay competition.
  • The prize is a new bicycle.
  • Sharing a gift with friends makes us enjoy it more.

mcqs.q: What did Hakeem win?
mcqs.why: Hakeem happily tells Ahmed that he won an essay competition.

mcqs.q: What is the first prize?
mcqs.why: Hakeem will get a new bicycle as the first prize in about a week.

mcqs.q: When will Hakeem get his prize?
mcqs.why: Hakeem says he will get the bicycle in about a week.

mcqs.q: What does Ahmed ask Hakeem?
options: If he will give him a ride
mcqs.why: Ahmed asks if Hakeem will give him a ride on the new bicycle.

mcqs.q: What does Hakeem reply to Ahmed?
mcqs.why: Hakeem says sure, because he wants to share his gift with his friend.

mcqs.q: Why does Hakeem want to share his gift?
options: He will not enjoy it if he does not share it with his friend
mcqs.why: Hakeem says he will not enjoy his gift if he does not share it with his friend.

mcqs.q: This dialogue teaches us to:
options: Express joy and share happiness with friends
mcqs.why: Practising this dialogue teaches us how to express joy and share happiness with friends.

mcqs.q: Who is happy in the dialogue?
mcqs.why: Hakeem is happy because he won the essay competition and the first prize.

mcqs.q: The essay competition prize is for:
mcqs.why: It is an essay competition, so the prize is for the best essay.

mcqs.q: Sharing our happiness with friends:
mcqs.why: Hakeem shares his gift with Ahmed because sharing makes us enjoy our gifts more.

lessons.title: 3.2 Reading - Postcards from Friends
lessons.notes_html:
The Four Provinces

Pakistan has four provinces: Punjab, Sindh, Balochistan and Khyber Pakhtunkhwa. Each province has its own regional dress, language and culture.

The Four Friends

Four students met at the All Pakistan Sports Olympiad, took part in the track races and became good friends.

  • Bilal - from Lahore (Punjab) - won the 100 metre race
  • Sher Ali - from Mardan (Khyber Pakhtunkhwa) - stood second in the 100 metre race
  • Khudadad - from Gwadar (Balochistan) - his team stood first in the relay race
  • Shankar - from Sukkur (Sindh) - won the 400 metre race

More Cities

  • Sindh: Karachi, Hyderabad
  • Balochistan: Quetta, Turbat
  • Punjab: Rawalpindi, Faisalabad
  • Khyber Pakhtunkhwa: Peshawar, Abbottabad

Postcards

Khudadad sent a postcard to Bilal. Shankar wrote a postcard to Sher Ali from Sukkur about the Sukkur Barrage. The children exchanged their addresses and telephone numbers and promised to keep in touch.

Key Points

  • Bilal is from Lahore, Sher Ali from Mardan, Khudadad from Gwadar and Shankar from Sukkur.
  • Shankar won the 400 metre race and was the star of them all.
  • Finding names in a text is called scanning for specific information.

mcqs.q: How many provinces does Pakistan have?
mcqs.why: Pakistan has four provinces: Punjab, Sindh, Balochistan and Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.

mcqs.q: Bilal is from:
mcqs.why: Bilal is from Lahore in Punjab. He won the 100 metre race.

mcqs.q: Sher Ali is from:
mcqs.why: Sher Ali is from Mardan in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa. He stood second in the 100 metre race.

mcqs.q: Khudadad is from:
mcqs.why: Khudadad is from Gwadar in Balochistan. His team stood first in the relay race.

mcqs.q: Shankar is from:
mcqs.why: Shankar is from Sukkur in Sindh. He won the 400 metre race.

mcqs.q: Who won the 400 metre race?
mcqs.why: Shankar won the 400 metre race and was the star of them all.

mcqs.q: Whose team stood first in the relay race?
mcqs.why: Khudadad's team stood first in the relay race, not Shankar's team.

mcqs.q: Where did the four students meet?
options: At the All Pakistan Sports Olympiad
mcqs.why: The four students met at the All Pakistan Sports Olympiad and became good friends.

mcqs.q: Which cities are in Sindh?
mcqs.why: Karachi and Hyderabad are cities of Sindh. Quetta is in Balochistan and Peshawar in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.

mcqs.q: What did Shankar write about in his postcard to Sher Ali?
mcqs.why: Shankar wrote a postcard to Sher Ali from Sukkur about the Sukkur Barrage.

lessons.title: 3.3 Writing - Notes on the Four Friends
lessons.notes_html:
Writing Short Notes

Short notes pick only the important facts from a table or text.

  • Sher Ali is from Mardan in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa. He stood second in the race. He received a postcard from Shankar.
  • Khudadad is from Gwadar in Balochistan. His team stood first in the relay race. He sent a postcard to Bilal.
  • Shankar is from Sukkur in Sindh. He won the 400 metre race. He sent a postcard to Sher Ali.

Sportsmanship - The Boat Race

  • The starter said: "Ready, steady, go!"
  • The people cheering shouted: "Come on! Fast!" and "Win the race, get ahead."
  • When one boat overturned, the people in it shouted: "Help! Help!"
  • The people in all the other boats said: "We must help them."
  • After helping, they all reached the finishing line together and said: "We won the race together."
  • All the people said: "You are true sportsmen."

True sportsmanship means helping others even in a competition.

Key Points

  • Short notes contain only the important facts.
  • The racers stopped to help the overturned boat.
  • True sportsmen help others even in a competition.

mcqs.q: Short notes pick out:
options: All the words of the text
mcqs.why: Short notes pick only the important facts from a table or text.

mcqs.q: Who received a postcard from Shankar?
mcqs.why: Shankar sent a postcard to Sher Ali, so Sher Ali received it.

mcqs.q: Who sent a postcard to Bilal?
mcqs.why: Khudadad sent a postcard to Bilal from Gwadar.

mcqs.q: Who said, "Ready, steady, go!" in the boat race?
mcqs.why: The starter said, "Ready, steady, go!" to begin the boat race.

mcqs.q: What did the people in the overturned boat shout?
mcqs.why: When one boat overturned, the people in it shouted, "Help! Help!"

mcqs.q: What did the people in the other boats say?
mcqs.why: The people in all the other boats said, "We must help them," and stopped to help.

mcqs.q: What did they say after reaching the finishing line together?
mcqs.why: After helping their friends, they all reached the finishing line together and said, "We won the race together."

mcqs.q: What did all the people say to the racers?
mcqs.why: All the people were very happy and said, "You are true sportsmen."

mcqs.q: True sportsmanship means:
options: Helping others even in a competition
mcqs.why: True sportsmanship means helping others even in a competition, like the racers helped the overturned boat.

mcqs.q: In the short note, Khudadad's team stood first in:
mcqs.why: Khudadad's team stood first in the relay race at the Sports Olympiad.

lessons.title: 3.3 Writing - How We Get Bread
lessons.notes_html:
From the Field to Our Table

Many people work so that we can eat bread. The sentences in the right order are:

  • Many people work so that we can eat bread.
  • The farmer works hard and grows the wheat.
  • The factory people buy the wheat and make flour.
  • The shopkeepers buy the flour from the factory.
  • We buy flour from the shopkeeper.
  • Finally, we make bread and eat it.

A paragraph joins ordered sentences together so that they read as one smooth piece of writing. It begins with a topic sentence and then gives details in order.

What Mother Does for Our Food

  • She gets up early in the morning.
  • She cleans the rice.
  • She cuts the vegetables.
  • She cooks the rice.
  • She makes curry.

Key Points

  • The farmer grows wheat; the factory makes flour.
  • We buy flour from the shopkeeper and make bread.
  • A paragraph has a topic sentence and details in order.

mcqs.q: Who grows the wheat?
mcqs.why: The farmer works hard and grows the wheat in his fields.

mcqs.q: Who makes flour from the wheat?
mcqs.why: The factory people buy the wheat and make flour from it.

mcqs.q: From whom do the shopkeepers buy the flour?
mcqs.why: The shopkeepers buy the flour from the factory and sell it in their shops.

mcqs.q: What is the last step in getting bread?
options: We make bread and eat it
mcqs.why: Finally, we make bread and eat it. It is the last step, from the field to our table.

mcqs.q: What does a paragraph do?
options: Joins ordered sentences into one smooth piece of writing
mcqs.why: A paragraph joins ordered sentences together so that they read as one smooth piece of writing.

mcqs.q: A paragraph begins with:
mcqs.why: A paragraph begins with a topic sentence and then gives details in order.

mcqs.q: What does mother do first so that our food is ready?
options: She gets up early in the morning
mcqs.why: The first sentence is: She gets up early in the morning. Then she cleans the rice and cuts the vegetables.

mcqs.q: What does mother do after cleaning the rice?
mcqs.why: The order is: cleans the rice, cuts the vegetables, cooks the rice, makes curry.

mcqs.q: Which sentence is the topic sentence of the mother paragraph?
options: My mother works hard to cook our food.
mcqs.why: "My mother works hard to cook our food" is the topic sentence; the other sentences give details.

mcqs.q: How many people work so that we can eat bread?
mcqs.why: The first sentence says: Many people work so that we can eat bread - the farmer, factory people and shopkeepers.

lessons.title: 3.4 Grammar - Is and Are with -ing Verbs
lessons.notes_html:
Making Sentences

We join a subject with is or are and an -ing verb to say what is happening now. Is is used with one person or thing, and are with more than one.

  • They are walking on the street.
  • We are eating bananas.
  • You are going to the mosque for prayers.
  • It is very busy in cleaning home.
  • He is reading the Holy Quran.
  • The cobbler is mending a pair of shoes.
  • The barber is cutting my hair.
  • Ahmed and Faraz are going to Larkana to visit their relatives.

Key Points

  • Is is used with one person or thing.
  • Are is used with more than one, and with we, you and they.
  • The main verb ends in -ing.

mcqs.q: The cobbler ___ mending a pair of shoes.
mcqs.why: The cobbler is one person, so we use "is": The cobbler is mending a pair of shoes.

mcqs.q: Ahmed and Faraz ___ going to Larkana.
mcqs.why: Ahmed and Faraz are two people, so we use "are" with more than one.

mcqs.q: They ___ walking on the street.
mcqs.why: With "they" we always use "are": They are walking on the street.

mcqs.q: He ___ reading the Holy Quran.
mcqs.why: He is one person, so we use "is": He is reading the Holy Quran.

mcqs.q: We ___ eating bananas.
mcqs.why: With "we" we use "are": We are eating bananas.

mcqs.q: The barber ___ cutting my hair.
mcqs.why: The barber is one person, so we use "is": The barber is cutting my hair.

mcqs.q: You ___ going to the mosque for prayers.
mcqs.why: With "you" we use "are": You are going to the mosque for prayers.

mcqs.q: In these sentences, the main verb ends in:
mcqs.why: The main verbs are walking, eating, going, reading, mending and cutting - they all end in -ing.

mcqs.q: Which sentence is correct?
mcqs.why: "It" takes "is", so "It is cleaning the home" is correct. They and we take "are", and he takes "is".

mcqs.q: "Is" is used with:
mcqs.why: "Is" is used with one person or thing, and "are" with more than one.

lessons.title: 3.4 Grammar - Routines with First, Next, Then
lessons.notes_html:
Bilquis's Morning

Linking words like first, next, then, after breakfast and finally show the order of events:

  • First, I get out of bed.
  • Next, I get dressed.
  • Then, I eat breakfast.
  • After breakfast, I brush my teeth and make my lunch.
  • Finally, I get on the bus and go to school.

Writing about a Friend's Routine

We ask questions in order: What is the first thing you do? What do you do next? After that, what do you do? What do you do finally? Then we write the answers as a paragraph.

He, She and -s Verbs

We use he for a boy and she for a girl. With one third person (he or she), we add s or es to the verb: she eats her lunch, she does her homework, he washes his hands.

Mother's Daily Routine

My mother gets up early, offers her prayers, prepares breakfast, helps us get ready for school, cleans the house, cooks food and helps us with our homework in the evening.

Key Points

  • First, next, then and finally show the order of a routine.
  • He is for a boy and she is for a girl.
  • With he or she, the verb takes s or es.

mcqs.q: What is the first thing Bilquis does in the morning?
mcqs.why: First, I get out of bed. Then she gets dressed and eats breakfast.

mcqs.q: What does Bilquis do after breakfast?
options: She brushes her teeth and makes her lunch
mcqs.why: After breakfast, I brush my teeth and make my lunch. Finally, she gets on the bus.

mcqs.q: What does Bilquis do finally?
options: She gets on the bus and goes to school
mcqs.why: Finally, I get on the bus and go to school. It is the last step of her morning.

mcqs.q: Linking words like first, next and finally show:
mcqs.why: Linking words like first, next, then and finally show the order of events in a story or routine.

mcqs.q: We use "she" for:
mcqs.why: We use "he" for a boy and "she" for a girl.

mcqs.q: Which sentence is correct?
mcqs.why: With "she", we add s to the verb: she eats, she does, he washes.

mcqs.q: "He ___ his hands before lunch." (wash)
mcqs.why: With "he", verbs ending in -sh take es: he washes his hands.

mcqs.q: In Sara's routine, what does she do after changing her clothes and washing her hands?
mcqs.why: After returning from school, Sara first changes her clothes and washes her hands. Then she eats her lunch.

mcqs.q: What does mother do in the evening?
options: She helps us with our homework
mcqs.why: In the evening, mother helps us with our homework and takes care of everyone.

mcqs.q: To describe a friend's routine, we first:
options: Ask questions in order and write the answers as a paragraph
mcqs.why: Asking questions in order and writing the answers as a paragraph is how we describe someone's routine.

lessons.title: 3.4 Grammar - Wh- Questions: What, Where, When
lessons.notes_html:
Three Question Words

  • What asks about a thing or an action.
  • Where asks about a place.
  • When asks about a time.

Examples

  • Sania is baking a cake in the kitchen in the morning. What is Sania doing? She is baking a cake. Where is she baking it? In the kitchen. When is she baking it? In the morning.
  • Asad is writing a letter in the class during his lesson.
  • Tahir is reading a book in the library in the afternoon.
  • Maryam is sewing a dress in the living room at night.
  • Zohra is playing a flute in the garden in the evening.

Questions for Given Answers

  • My book is in my bag. - Where is your book?
  • I am going to Lahore tomorrow. - When are you going to Lahore?
  • I am eating a mango. - What are you eating?

Key Points

  • What asks about a thing, where about a place, when about a time.
  • The answer to a where-question is a place.
  • The answer to a when-question is a time.

mcqs.q: "___ is Sania doing?" - She is baking a cake.
mcqs.why: "What" asks about an action or a thing: What is Sania doing? She is baking a cake.

mcqs.q: "___ is Tahir reading a book?" - In the library.
mcqs.why: "Where" asks about a place. The library is a place.

mcqs.q: "___ is Zohra playing a flute?" - In the evening.
mcqs.why: "When" asks about a time. In the evening is a time.

mcqs.q: Maryam is sewing a dress. What is Maryam doing?
mcqs.why: The sentence says Maryam is sewing a dress in the living room at night.

mcqs.q: Asad is writing a letter during his lesson. When is he writing it?
mcqs.why: "During his lesson" tells the time, so it answers the question "When?"

mcqs.q: "My book is in my bag." The question for this answer is:
mcqs.why: The answer gives a place (in my bag), so the question begins with "Where".

mcqs.q: "I am going to Lahore tomorrow." The question is:
options: When are you going to Lahore?
mcqs.why: The word "tomorrow" tells the time, so the question begins with "When".

mcqs.q: "I am eating a mango." The question is:
mcqs.why: A mango is a thing, so the question begins with "What": What are you eating?

mcqs.q: Tahir is reading a book in the library. Where is he reading?
mcqs.why: "In the library" is a place, so it answers the where-question.

mcqs.q: Which question word asks about a time?
mcqs.why: "When" asks about a time, like in the morning, in the evening or tomorrow.

lessons.title: 3.4 Grammar - Wh- Questions: Who and Why
lessons.notes_html:
Two More Question Words

  • Who asks about a person.
  • Why asks about a reason. Its answer usually begins with because.

Examples

  • Who is baking a cake? Sania is baking a cake. Why is she baking it? Because it is her sister's birthday.
  • Asad is writing a letter because he has to finish his classwork.
  • Tahir is reading a book because he has to do homework.
  • Maryam is sewing a dress because she wants to wear it at a wedding.
  • Zohra is playing a flute because she is learning to play it.

Questions for Given Answers

  • I am laughing because I am happy. - Why are you laughing?
  • My best friend is my mother. - Who is your best friend?
  • I am doing my homework. - What are you doing?

Key Points

  • Who asks about a person; why asks about a reason.
  • Why-answers often begin with because.
  • Each question begins with a different wh- word.

mcqs.q: "___ is baking a cake?" - Sania is baking a cake.
mcqs.why: "Who" asks about a person. Sania is a person.

mcqs.q: "___ is Sania baking a cake?" - Because it is her sister's birthday.
mcqs.why: "Why" asks about a reason, and the answer begins with "because".

mcqs.q: Why is Asad writing a letter?
options: Because he has to finish his classwork
mcqs.why: Asad is writing a letter because he has to finish his classwork.

mcqs.q: Who is reading a book?
mcqs.why: Tahir is reading a book in the library because he has to do homework.

mcqs.q: Why is Maryam sewing a dress?
options: Because she wants to wear it at a wedding
mcqs.why: Maryam is sewing a dress because she wants to wear it at a wedding.

mcqs.q: "I am laughing because I am happy." The question is:
mcqs.why: The answer gives a reason with "because", so the question begins with "Why".

mcqs.q: "My best friend is my mother." The question is:
mcqs.why: The answer names a person, so the question begins with "Who".

mcqs.q: Why is Zohra playing a flute?
options: Because she is learning to play it
mcqs.why: Zohra is playing a flute because she is learning to play it.

mcqs.q: Which question word asks about a reason?
mcqs.why: "Why" asks about a reason, and its answer usually begins with "because".

mcqs.q: Why is Tahir reading a book?
options: Because he has to do homework
mcqs.why: Tahir is reading a book because he has to do homework.

lessons.title: 3.5 Study Skills - City, Village and Ordinal Numbers
lessons.notes_html:
Related Words

  • City: buildings, roads, cars, shops, schools, hospitals, traffic
  • Village: fields, farms, animals, wells, huts, trees, farmers

In alphabetical order: Animals, buildings, cars, farms, farmers, fields, hospitals, huts, roads, schools, shops, traffic, trees, wells. When first letters are the same, we look at the second letter, as in farms before farmers.

Ordinal Numbers

Ordinal numbers tell us the position of something in a line: first - 1st, second - 2nd, third - 3rd, fourth - 4th, fifth - 5th, sixth - 6th, seventh - 7th, eighth - 8th, ninth - 9th, tenth - 10th.

To find the ordinal number of a grey star, count the stars from the left and write its position in words and figures, like 7th - Seventh.

Key Points

  • City words and village words are grouped by topic.
  • Alphabetical order uses first letters, then second letters.
  • Ordinal numbers show position: first, second, third.

mcqs.q: Which word is related to "city"?
mcqs.why: Traffic is a city word, with buildings, roads, cars, shops, schools and hospitals.

mcqs.q: Which word is related to "village"?
mcqs.why: Farms is a village word, with fields, animals, wells, huts, trees and farmers.

mcqs.q: In alphabetical order, which comes first: farms or farmers?
mcqs.why: Both start with "farm", but farms ends there while farmers has more letters; also by second letters, farms comes before farmers in the list.

mcqs.q: Ordinal numbers tell us:
options: The position of something in a line
mcqs.why: Ordinal numbers tell us the position of something in a line, like first, second and third.

mcqs.q: Which is the ordinal number for 5th?
mcqs.why: 5th is written in words as fifth. Five is the counting number.

mcqs.q: Second is written in figures as:
mcqs.why: First - 1st, second - 2nd, third - 3rd and fourth - 4th.

mcqs.q: Which ordinal number comes after sixth?
mcqs.why: The order is: fifth, sixth, seventh, eighth, ninth, tenth. So seventh comes after sixth.

mcqs.q: Tenth is written in figures as:
mcqs.why: Tenth - 10th. Ninth is 9th and eighth is 8th.

mcqs.q: To find the ordinal number of a grey star, we:
options: Count the stars from the left and write its position
mcqs.why: Count the stars from the left and write the position of each grey star in words and figures, like 7th - Seventh.

mcqs.q: Which comes first in alphabetical order: animals or buildings?
mcqs.why: Animals starts with A and buildings with B, so animals comes first in alphabetical order.

lessons.title: 3.6 Fun - Spot the Difference and Teacher Says
lessons.notes_html:
Spot the Differences

This is a picture activity. Look at the two pictures side by side with your partner and say what is different in each one. There are 4 differences to find, for example a missing object, a different colour, a changed shape or an extra thing in one picture. The exact differences can only be read from the pictures in the book.

The Game "Teacher Says"

  • When the teacher says an animal, jump forward.
  • When the teacher says a flower, clap your hands.
  • When the teacher says a fruit, jump backwards.
  • When the teacher says a colour, stamp your feet.
  • When the teacher says a dress, click your fingers.

But we only do the action when the teacher says "Teacher says" first. This game trains listening and quick action.

Key Points

  • There are 4 differences between the two pictures.
  • In Teacher Says, act only when the teacher says "Teacher says" first.
  • The game trains listening and quick action.

mcqs.q: How many differences are there between the two pictures?
mcqs.why: There are 4 differences between the two pictures, and we find them by looking at both pictures side by side.

mcqs.q: Which of these can be a difference between the pictures?
mcqs.why: A difference can be a missing object, a different colour, a changed shape or an extra thing in one picture.

mcqs.q: In "Teacher Says", when the teacher names an animal, we:
mcqs.why: When the teacher says the name of an animal, we jump forward.

mcqs.q: When the teacher names a flower, we:
mcqs.why: When the teacher says a flower, we clap our hands.

mcqs.q: When the teacher names a fruit, we:
mcqs.why: When the teacher says a fruit, we jump backwards.

mcqs.q: When the teacher names a colour, we:
mcqs.why: When the teacher says a colour, we stamp our feet.

mcqs.q: When the teacher names a dress, we:
mcqs.why: When the teacher says a dress, we click our fingers.

mcqs.q: We do the action only when:
mcqs.why: We only perform the action when the teacher says "Teacher says" first.

mcqs.q: This game trains:
mcqs.why: The game "Teacher Says" trains listening and quick action.

mcqs.q: To spot the differences, we look at the two pictures:
options: One by one, on different days
mcqs.why: We look at the two pictures side by side with a partner and say what is different in each one.

lessons.title: 4.1 Oral Communication - Buying Shoes
lessons.notes_html:
The Dialogue

This is an oral dialogue between Ayesha and Bano at a shoe shop. We practise it with a partner.

What Happens

  • Ayesha asks the shopkeeper uncle to show the brown shoes, but Bano thinks the size is too big.
  • Ayesha suggests the red shoes, but Bano thinks the colour is too bright.
  • At last, Bano likes the grey pair.
  • Ayesha says they will buy these shoes.

Why We Practise It

Practising this dialogue teaches us how to express opinion and politely agree or disagree while shopping.

Key Points

  • The brown shoes were too big and the red shoes too bright.
  • Bano liked the grey pair at last.
  • We can disagree politely while shopping.

mcqs.q: Where does the dialogue "Buying Shoes" take place?
mcqs.why: Ayesha and Bano are at a shoe shop, and Ayesha asks the shopkeeper to show them shoes.

mcqs.q: Which shoes does Ayesha ask to see first?
mcqs.why: Ayesha asks the shopkeeper uncle to show the brown shoes first.

mcqs.q: What is wrong with the brown shoes?
mcqs.why: Bano thinks the size of the brown shoes is too big.

mcqs.q: What is wrong with the red shoes?
mcqs.why: Bano thinks the colour of the red shoes is too bright.

mcqs.q: Which pair does Bano like at last?
mcqs.why: At last, Bano likes the grey pair, and Ayesha says they will buy these shoes.

mcqs.q: What does Ayesha say at the end?
options: They do not like any shoes
mcqs.why: When Bano likes the grey pair, Ayesha says they will buy these shoes.

mcqs.q: This dialogue teaches us to:
options: Express opinion and politely agree or disagree while shopping
mcqs.why: Practising this dialogue teaches us how to express opinion and politely agree or disagree while shopping.

mcqs.q: Who thinks the brown shoes are too big?
mcqs.why: Bano thinks the size of the brown shoes is too big and their colour choice is too bright in red.

mcqs.q: Bano's opinion about the red shoes is that:
mcqs.why: Ayesha suggests the red shoes, but Bano thinks the colour is too bright.

mcqs.q: The shopkeeper is called:
mcqs.why: Ayesha asks the shopkeeper uncle to show the brown shoes. Children politely call him uncle.

lessons.title: 4.2 Reading - Mountains, Rivers and Streams
lessons.notes_html:
Box 1: Mountains and Hills

Mountains and hills are high above the ground. A mountain is higher and steeper than a hill. The high mountains have snow on their peaks. The highest peaks in the world are Mount Everest and K-2. K-2 is in Pakistan.

Box 2: Rivers and Streams

A river is a bit broader than a stream. Small streams join with others to form a river. The River Indus is the largest river in Pakistan. The river Nile is the largest river in Egypt.

Who Am I?

  • Way above the ground and steeper than a hill - a mountain
  • In Pakistan and one of the highest peaks - K-2
  • Flows fast and is larger than a stream - a river
  • Joins with others to form a river - a stream
  • A river in Egypt - the river Nile
  • A river in Pakistan - the river Indus

Key Points

  • A mountain is higher and steeper than a hill.
  • K-2 is in Pakistan; Everest and K-2 are the highest peaks.
  • The Indus is the largest river of Pakistan and the Nile of Egypt.

mcqs.q: Box 1 of the text tells us about:
mcqs.why: Box 1 describes mountains and hills, which are high above the ground.

mcqs.q: A mountain is ___ than a hill.
mcqs.why: A mountain is higher and steeper than a hill, and high mountains have snow on their peaks.

mcqs.q: What do the high mountains have on their peaks?
mcqs.why: The high mountains have snow on their peaks.

mcqs.q: The highest peaks in the world are:
mcqs.why: The highest peaks in the world are Mount Everest and K-2. K-2 is in Pakistan.

mcqs.q: K-2 is in:
mcqs.why: K-2 is in Pakistan and is one of the highest peaks in the world.

mcqs.q: A river is a bit ___ than a stream.
mcqs.why: A river is a bit broader than a stream, and small streams join to form a river.

mcqs.q: When small streams join with others, they form a:
mcqs.why: When streams join with others, they form a river.

mcqs.q: The largest river of Pakistan is:
mcqs.why: The River Indus is the largest river in Pakistan. The Nile is in Egypt.

mcqs.q: The river Nile is in:
mcqs.why: The river Nile is the largest river in Egypt.

mcqs.q: "I am way above the ground, I am steeper than a hill." Who am I?
mcqs.why: A mountain is way above the ground and steeper than a hill.

lessons.title: 4.2 Reading - Seas, Ports and the Uses of Rivers
lessons.notes_html:
Box 3: The Use of Rivers

A river gives us water for drinking, cooking and washing. A river has a lot of fish in it, and people fish along the bank of the river. People use rowing boats and ferries to cross the river. When a river overflows, it can cause a flood.

Box 4: Seas and Oceans

The mouth of the river is where it slowly falls into the sea. The seas and oceans have salty water. The River Indus falls into the Arabian Sea.

Box 5: Sea Ports

At the sea port, the water is deep. Pakistan has three main ports: Karachi Port, Port Qasim and Gwadar Port. The largest port of Pakistan is Karachi Port.

Key Points

  • Rivers give us water and fish; boats and ferries cross them.
  • The Indus falls into the Arabian Sea.
  • Pakistan has three main ports; Karachi Port is the largest.

mcqs.q: Box 3 of the text tells us about:
mcqs.why: Box 3 tells us how rivers give us water, fish and transport.

mcqs.q: A river gives us water for:
mcqs.why: A river gives us water for drinking, cooking and washing.

mcqs.q: People use ___ to cross the river.
mcqs.why: People use rowing boats and ferries to cross the river.

mcqs.q: When a river overflows, it can cause a:
mcqs.why: When a river overflows, it can cause flood.

mcqs.q: The mouth of the river is:
options: Where it slowly falls into the sea
The deepest part of the sea
mcqs.why: The mouth of the river is where it slowly falls into the sea.

mcqs.q: The seas and oceans have:
mcqs.why: Box 4 tells us that the seas and oceans have salty water.

mcqs.q: The River Indus falls into the:
mcqs.why: The River Indus falls into the Arabian Sea, which is the sea near Pakistan.

mcqs.q: How many main ports does Pakistan have?
mcqs.why: Pakistan has three main ports: Karachi Port, Port Qasim and Gwadar Port.

mcqs.q: The largest port of Pakistan is:
mcqs.why: The largest port of Pakistan is Karachi Port.

mcqs.q: At the sea port, the water is:
mcqs.why: Box 5 describes the seaport and tells us that at the sea port, the water is deep.

lessons.title: 4.3 Writing - Contractions
lessons.notes_html:
What is a Contraction?

A contraction joins two words into one short form with an apostrophe. For example, "we have" becomes "we've".

Short Forms

  • We have - We've (We've finished our food.)
  • I have - I've (I've seen you before.)
  • There is - There's (There's a river.)
  • I do not - I don't (I don't know about China.)
  • She did not - She didn't (She didn't do this.)
  • I am - I'm (I'm doing my home work.)
  • This is not - This isn't (This isn't the book I want.)
  • We are not - We aren't (We aren't going to the shop.)

Key Points

  • A contraction is a short form of two words.
  • An apostrophe shows where letters are left out.
  • Do not becomes don't; did not becomes didn't.

mcqs.q: What is a contraction?
options: A long form of a word
Two words joined into one short form with an apostrophe
mcqs.why: A contraction joins two words into one short form with an apostrophe, like "we have" becomes "we've".

mcqs.q: The short form of "we have" is:
mcqs.why: "We have" becomes "we've": We've finished our food.

mcqs.q: "I have seen you before" in short form is:
mcqs.why: "I have" becomes "I've", so the sentence is: I've seen you before.

mcqs.q: The short form of "there is" is:
mcqs.why: "There is" becomes "there's": There's a river.

mcqs.q: "I do not know about China" in short form is:
mcqs.why: "Do not" becomes "don't": I don't know about China.

mcqs.q: The short form of "did not" is:
mcqs.why: "Did not" becomes "didn't": She didn't do this.

mcqs.q: "I am doing my home work" in short form is:
mcqs.why: "I am" becomes "I'm": I'm doing my home work.

mcqs.q: "This is not the book I want" - the contraction is:
options: This isn't the book I want
mcqs.why: "Is not" becomes "isn't": This isn't the book I want.

mcqs.q: "We are not going to the shop" in short form is:
options: We aren't going to the shop
We isn't going to the shop
We don't going to the shop
We won't going to the shop
mcqs.why: "Are not" becomes "aren't": We aren't going to the shop.

mcqs.q: In a contraction, the apostrophe shows:
mcqs.why: The apostrophe takes the place of the letters that are left out, like the "ha" in we've.

lessons.title: 4.3 Writing - The Mouse and the Lion
lessons.notes_html:
A Trip to the Zoo

Anum asks Aleeza about her trip to the zoo. Aleeza saw five big brown monkeys. She also saw lions, elephants and colourful birds. It was a happy and exciting trip.

The Story: The Mouse and the Lion

One day, a mouse was playing in the jungle. A lion was sleeping there. The mouse did not see it and ran over the lion's foot. The lion woke up and caught the mouse.

  • The lion said: "You have disturbed my sleep." "Now I'm going to eat you." "Why should I let you go?" "How can a small mouse help a big lion?"
  • The mouse said: "I'm sorry. I didn't see you." "Please don't eat me. Please let me go." "I may be able to help you some time." "I don't know but I promise I'll help you."

The lion laughed but let the mouse go. A few days later, the lion was caught in a hunter's trap. The little mouse cut the rope with his sharp teeth and the lion was free. "Thank you, little mouse, for saving my life," said the lion.

Key Points

  • The lion let the mouse go when the mouse promised to help him.
  • The mouse saved the lion by cutting the rope of the trap.
  • Even a small friend can help a big friend one day.

mcqs.q: Where did Aleeza go on her trip?
mcqs.why: Anum asks Aleeza, "How was your trip to the zoo?" so the trip was to the zoo.

mcqs.q: What did Aleeza see first at the zoo?
mcqs.why: Aleeza said, "I saw five big brown monkeys. They were big and fat."

mcqs.q: What else did Aleeza see at the zoo?
mcqs.why: Aleeza also saw lions, elephants and colourful birds, and enjoyed the trip very much.

mcqs.q: In the story, what was the lion doing when the mouse came?
mcqs.why: A lion was sleeping in the jungle. The mouse ran over its foot and disturbed its sleep.

mcqs.q: What did the mouse run over?
mcqs.why: The mouse did not see the lion and ran over the lion's foot, so the lion woke up and caught it.

mcqs.q: What did the mouse promise the lion?
mcqs.why: The mouse said, "I may be able to help you some time," and promised to help the lion.

mcqs.q: Why did the lion let the mouse go?
options: He was not hungry and the mouse promised to help him
He was afraid of the mouse
mcqs.why: The lion laughed but let the mouse go after the mouse said sorry and promised to help him some time.

mcqs.q: How was the lion caught later?
mcqs.why: A few days later, the lion was caught in a hunter's trap.

mcqs.q: How did the mouse free the lion?
options: He cut the rope with his sharp teeth
mcqs.why: The little mouse cut the rope with his sharp teeth and the lion was free.

mcqs.q: What does this story teach us?
options: Even a small friend can help a big friend one day
mcqs.why: The story teaches us that even a small friend can help a big friend one day.

lessons.title: 4.4 Grammar - Adjectives of Size and Colour
lessons.notes_html:
What is an Adjective?

Adjectives are words that describe a noun. They tell us about its size, colour and other qualities, like "a long shirt" or "a long, white shirt".

From the Dialogue "In an Art Classroom"

  • Birds - tiny, yellow
  • Tree - tall, green
  • River - large, blue
  • Sea - calm, blue
  • Mountains - huge, snow-covered
  • Streams - small, white

Describing Our Things

  • My bag is big and red. My pencil is small and yellow.
  • My house is large and white. My hair is short and black.
  • My friend has a small blue bag and a long green pencil.

Key Points

  • Adjectives describe nouns: size, colour and quality.
  • Tiny, tall, large, huge and small are size adjectives.
  • Yellow, green, blue and white are colour adjectives.

mcqs.q: An adjective is a word that:
mcqs.why: Adjectives are words that describe a noun, telling us about its size, colour and other qualities.

mcqs.q: In the art classroom dialogue, the birds are:
mcqs.why: The table from the dialogue says: Birds - tiny, yellow.

mcqs.q: The mountains are described as:
mcqs.why: Mountains - huge (size), snow-covered (quality). The sea is calm and blue.

mcqs.q: The streams are:
mcqs.why: From the dialogue table: Streams - small (size), white (colour).

mcqs.q: Which pair gives the size and colour of the river?
mcqs.why: River - large (size), blue (colour), as completed from the dialogue.

mcqs.q: "My bag is big and red." The adjectives are:
mcqs.why: Big describes the size and red describes the colour of the bag, so both are adjectives.

mcqs.q: Which word is a size adjective?
mcqs.why: Huge tells the size. Yellow, green and blue are colour adjectives.

mcqs.q: Which word is a colour adjective?
mcqs.why: White is a colour. Tall, small and tiny tell the size.

mcqs.q: "My friend has a long green pencil." The adjectives describe:
mcqs.why: Long (size) and green (colour) describe the pencil.

mcqs.q: Describing things with size and colour adjectives makes our speaking and writing:
mcqs.why: Describing things with size and colour adjectives makes our speaking and writing clear and interesting.

lessons.title: 4.4 Grammar - Degrees of Adjectives
lessons.notes_html:
Three Degrees

Adjectives have three degrees: positive (tall), comparative (taller) and superlative (tallest). We use the comparative to compare two things and the superlative for the most of all.

Examples

  • Ahmed is a tall boy. Ahmed is taller than Shiraz. Sameer is the tallest boy.
  • The apple tree is big. It is bigger than the guava tree. The mango tree is the biggest.
  • This bulb is bright. The moon is brighter than a bulb. The sun is the brightest.
  • This is a small black duck. The white duck is smaller. The pink duck is the smallest.
  • A kite is flying high. A bird is flying higher. An airplane is flying at the highest level.
  • Asiya has long hair. Asma has longer hair. Anum has the longest hair.

Key Points

  • Positive: tall, big, bright, small, high, long.
  • Comparative adds -er and is used with "than".
  • Superlative adds -est and is used with "the".

mcqs.q: The three degrees of adjectives are:
mcqs.why: The three degrees are: positive (tall), comparative (taller) and superlative (tallest).

mcqs.q: Ahmed is ___ than Shiraz.
mcqs.why: We compare two boys, so we use the comparative: Ahmed is taller than Shiraz.

mcqs.q: Sameer is the ___ boy.
mcqs.why: For the most of all we use the superlative with "the": Sameer is the tallest boy.

mcqs.q: The mango tree is the ___ of the three trees.
