mcqs.why: The apple tree is big, bigger than the guava tree, and the mango tree is the biggest.

mcqs.q: The moon is ___ than a bulb.
mcqs.why: We compare the moon with a bulb, so we use the comparative: brighter than a bulb.

mcqs.q: The sun is the ___ of all.
mcqs.why: The sun is the brightest. The superlative is used with "the" for the most of all.

mcqs.q: The pink duck is the ___ duck.
mcqs.why: The black duck is small, the white duck is smaller, and the pink duck is the smallest.

mcqs.q: An airplane is flying at the ___ level.
mcqs.why: A kite flies high, a bird flies higher, and an airplane flies at the highest level.

mcqs.q: Asma has ___ hair than Asiya.
mcqs.why: Asiya has long hair, Asma has longer hair than Asiya, and Anum has the longest hair.

mcqs.q: The comparative degree is used:
mcqs.why: The comparative (taller, bigger) compares two things and is used with "than".

lessons.title: 4.5 Study Skills - Sky and Land Words
lessons.notes_html:
Related Words

  • Sky: sun, moon, stars, clouds, birds, rainbow, aeroplane
  • Land: fields, mountains, rivers, roads, houses, trees, farms

Grouping words by topic helps us build vocabulary for speaking and writing.

Alphabetical Order

Aeroplane, birds, clouds, farms, fields, houses, moon, mountains, rainbow, rivers, roads, stars, sun, trees. Words are arranged from A to Z by their first letters.

Making Sentences

We can make meaningful sentences from mixed words: "She is happy." "The car is fast." "Birds fly over the tree." "I have seen a peacock." "Yes, please be quiet in the park."

Key Points

  • Sky words: sun, moon, stars, clouds, birds, rainbow, aeroplane.
  • Land words: fields, mountains, rivers, roads, houses, trees, farms.
  • Alphabetical order arranges words from A to Z.

mcqs.q: Which word is related to "Sky"?
mcqs.why: Rainbow is a sky word, with sun, moon, stars, clouds, birds and aeroplane.

mcqs.q: Which word is related to "Land"?
mcqs.why: Fields is a land word, with mountains, rivers, roads, houses, trees and farms.

mcqs.q: Which word comes first in alphabetical order?
mcqs.why: Aeroplane starts with A, so it comes first in alphabetical order.

mcqs.q: In alphabetical order, which comes first: rivers or roads?
mcqs.why: Both start with R, but the second letter of rivers is "i" and of roads is "o"; i comes before o, so rivers comes first.

mcqs.q: Which is a meaningful sentence from the given words?
mcqs.why: "Birds fly over the tree" is a meaningful sentence made from the word set in the exercise.

mcqs.q: Grouping words by topic helps us to:
options: Build vocabulary for speaking and writing
mcqs.why: Grouping words by topic helps us build vocabulary for speaking and writing.

mcqs.q: Which of these is a sky word?
mcqs.why: An aeroplane flies in the sky, so it is grouped with sky words.

mcqs.q: Which word comes last in alphabetical order: sun, moon, trees, birds?
mcqs.why: T comes after B, M and S in the alphabet, so trees comes last.

mcqs.q: "I have seen a peacock" is made from which word set's words?
options: really, please, yes, quiet, seen, a, park, peacock, be, you, have, my
a, it, the, she, is, we
mcqs.why: The words I, have, seen, a and peacock all come from the fourth word set in the exercise.

mcqs.q: In alphabetical order, "mountains" comes:
mcqs.why: Moon and mountains both start with "mo", but the third letter of moon is "o" and of mountains is "u"; o comes before u, so mountains comes after moon.

lessons.title: 4.6 Fun - Riddles with Adjectives
lessons.notes_html:
Fun with Adjectives - Riddles

A riddle describes a thing with adjectives, and we guess what it is.

  • Something hard with four legs - a table
  • Something with three long arms that goes round and round - a fan
  • Something round with a white plate and 2 spoons on it - a clock
  • Something like a small room with 100 soldiers wearing the same coloured helmet - a matchbox

Think, Play and Say!

Student A says, "I can see in front of me something beginning with 'b'." The others guess: "Is it a boy?" "Is it a bulb?" Student A answers, "Yes, it is" or "No, it isn't", until someone guesses correctly. This game practises the alphabet, vocabulary and yes/no answers.

Key Points

  • Riddles use adjectives to describe things.
  • The fan has three arms; the clock has two hands like spoons.
  • The guessing game answers are "Yes, it is" and "No, it isn't".

mcqs.q: Riddle: "I can see something hard and it has four legs." What is it?
mcqs.why: A table is hard and has four legs, exactly as the riddle describes it.

mcqs.q: Riddle: "It has long three arms. It goes round and round." What is it?
mcqs.why: A fan has three long blades or arms and goes round and round.

mcqs.q: Riddle: "Something round with a white plate. It has 2 spoons on it." What is it?
mcqs.why: A clock is round with a white face like a plate and has two hands like spoons.

mcqs.q: Riddle: "Like a small room with 100 soldiers wearing the same coloured helmet." What is it?
mcqs.why: A matchbox is like a small room full of matches, and the matches look like soldiers with the same coloured helmets.

mcqs.q: Riddles are a fun way to use:
mcqs.why: Riddles are a fun way to use adjectives to describe things.

mcqs.q: In the guessing game, Student A says the thing begins with:
mcqs.why: Student A says, "I can see in front of me something beginning with 'b'." The letter is the clue.

mcqs.q: What do the other students do in the game?
options: They guess: "Is it a boy?" "Is it a bulb?"
mcqs.why: The others guess with yes/no questions like "Is it a boy?" or "Is it a bulb?"

mcqs.q: Student A answers the guesses with:
mcqs.why: Student A answers, "Yes, it is," or "No, it isn't," until someone guesses correctly.

mcqs.q: This game practises:
options: The alphabet, vocabulary and yes/no answers
mcqs.why: This game practises the alphabet, vocabulary and yes/no answers.

mcqs.q: The clock's two hands are compared with:
mcqs.why: The riddle says the clock has 2 spoons on it - its two hands look like spoons.

lessons.title: 5.1 Oral Communication - In the Classroom
lessons.notes_html:
The Dialogue

This is an oral dialogue between a teacher and her students in the classroom. We practise it with a partner.

What Happens

  • Gulnaz asks, "May I come in, please?" and the teacher says, "Yes, you may."
  • Mahnoor asks, "May I go to the washroom?" and the teacher says, "No. Wait till the bell rings."
  • Munira asks, "Teacher, can I also go when the bell rings?" and the teacher says, "Yes, you can."

Why We Practise It

Practising this dialogue teaches us how to seek permission politely with may and can.

Key Points

  • We use "may" and "can" to ask for permission politely.
  • Gulnaz is allowed to come in.
  • Mahnoor must wait till the bell rings.

mcqs.q: Who asks, "May I come in, please?"
mcqs.why: Gulnaz asks, "May I come in, please?" and the teacher says, "Yes, you may."

mcqs.q: What does the teacher say to Gulnaz?
mcqs.why: The teacher gives Gulnaz permission and says, "Yes, you may."

mcqs.q: What does Mahnoor ask?
options: May I go to the washroom?
mcqs.why: Mahnoor asks, "May I go to the washroom?" but the teacher asks her to wait.

mcqs.q: Why can Mahnoor not go at once?
options: She must wait till the bell rings
mcqs.why: The teacher says, "No. Wait till the bell rings."

mcqs.q: What does Munira ask the teacher?
options: Can I also go when the bell rings?
mcqs.why: Munira asks, "Teacher, can I also go when the bell rings?" and the teacher says, "Yes, you can."

mcqs.q: What does the teacher say to Munira?
mcqs.why: The teacher allows Munira and says, "Yes, you can."

mcqs.q: We ask for permission politely with:
mcqs.why: This dialogue teaches us how to seek permission politely with "may" and "can".

mcqs.q: Where does this dialogue take place?
mcqs.why: The dialogue is called "In the Classroom" and happens between a teacher and her students.

mcqs.q: Who must wait till the bell rings?
mcqs.why: The teacher tells Mahnoor to wait till the bell rings before going to the washroom.

mcqs.q: Asking "May I come in, please?" shows that we are:
mcqs.why: Using "may" and "please" is a polite way to seek permission.

lessons.title: 5.2 Reading - My Family
lessons.notes_html:
Husna's Family

There are 7 people in Husna's family: mother, father, Husna, Hammad, Fatima, Rafay and grandmother. There are 4 females (mother, Husna, Fatima, grandmother) and 3 males (father, Hammad, Rafay).

Mother's Busy Day

  • Mother gets up early in the morning and prepares breakfast after morning prayers.
  • Father drops the children to school and then goes to work.
  • Mother gives Rafay a bath, waters the plants and cooks lunch at 11 o'clock. She is a good cook.
  • Grandmother is weak and old. She likes tea and rusks for breakfast.
  • Children do their homework with mother. She allows them to play in the evening, after their homework.
  • After father returns, the family has dinner together and shares the activities of the day. They go to bed early because they get up early.
  • Parro (the parrot) likes to eat green chillies.

Five Duties of Husna's Mother

She prepares breakfast, gives Rafay a bath, waters the plants, cooks tasty food and helps the children do their homework.

Key Points

  • Husna's family has 7 people: 4 females and 3 males.
  • Mother works all day to take care of the family.
  • The family sleeps early and gets up early.

mcqs.q: How many people are there in Husna's family?
mcqs.why: There are 7 people: mother, father, Husna, Hammad, Fatima, Rafay and grandmother.

mcqs.q: How many females are in Husna's family?
mcqs.why: There are 4 females: mother, Husna, Fatima and grandmother.

mcqs.q: How many males are in Husna's family?
mcqs.why: There are 3 males: father, Hammad and Rafay.

mcqs.q: When does mother get up?
mcqs.why: Mother gets up early in the morning and prepares breakfast after morning prayers.

mcqs.q: Who drops the children to school?
mcqs.why: Father gets ready, drops the children to school and then goes to work.

mcqs.q: At what time does mother cook lunch?
mcqs.why: The text says mother cooks lunch at 11 o'clock.

mcqs.q: Mother is a good:
mcqs.why: The correct answer from the text is "cook": Mother is a good cook.

mcqs.q: What does grandmother like for breakfast?
mcqs.why: Grandmother likes tea and rusks for breakfast. She is weak and old.

mcqs.q: When does mother allow the children to go out to play?
options: In the evening, after they have done their homework
mcqs.why: Mother allows the children to go out to play in the evening, after they have done their homework.

mcqs.q: What does Parro like to eat?
mcqs.why: Parro, the parrot, likes to eat green chillies.

lessons.title: 5.3 Writing - Invitation Cards
lessons.notes_html:
An Invitation Card

An invitation card must show who is invited, the purpose, the date, the time, the venue and who sends it. It can be made colourful with drawings.

Example: "Dear Ali, You are invited to our Eid Milan party. Date: 12-04-2018. Time: 4:00pm-6:00pm. Venue: Class IV, School Hall. From: Sara."

A Thank-You Reply

A reply to an invitation says thanks, says whether we will come, and ends with love and our name. Maha writes to Zara: "I am so excited about your doll's wedding. I will come. I will bring my dolls and mithai for everyone. Thank you and see you soon. Love, Maha."

A Roza Kushai Invitation

A Roza Kushai is held when a child observes his first fast (roza). Sara invites her cousin Ahmed to her little brother Ali's Roza Kushai. Ahmed replies with thanks and promises to come and bring a gift.

Key Points

  • An invitation card shows the person invited, purpose, date, time, venue and sender.
  • A good reply thanks the sender and accepts the invitation.
  • Roza Kushai celebrates a child's first fast.

mcqs.q: An invitation card must show:
options: Who is invited, the purpose, date, time, venue and who sends it
mcqs.why: An invitation card must show who is invited, the purpose, the date, the time, the venue and who sends it.

mcqs.q: In Sara's Eid Milan card, the venue is:
mcqs.why: Sara's card says: Venue: Class IV, School Hall. Date: 12-04-2018, Time: 4:00pm-6:00pm.

mcqs.q: What is the time of the Eid Milan party in the example?
mcqs.why: The example card gives the time as 4:00pm-6:00pm.

mcqs.q: A reply to an invitation should:
options: Say thanks and say whether we will come
mcqs.why: A reply to an invitation says thanks, says whether we will come, and ends with love and our name.

mcqs.q: What will Maha bring to Zara's doll's wedding?
options: Her dolls and mithai for everyone
mcqs.why: Maha writes: I will bring my dolls and "mithai" for everyone.

mcqs.q: A Roza Kushai is held when:
options: A child observes his first fast
mcqs.why: A Roza Kushai is held when a child observes his first fast (roza), like Sara's little brother Ali.

mcqs.q: Who invites Ahmed to the Roza Kushai?
mcqs.why: Sara writes a note to her cousin Ahmed to invite him to her little brother Ali's Roza Kushai.

mcqs.q: What will Ahmed bring to the Roza Kushai?
mcqs.why: Ahmed replies that he is very happy for Ali and will bring a gift for him.

mcqs.q: How does a thank-you reply usually end?
mcqs.why: A reply ends with love and our name, like "Love, Maha" or "Love, Ahmed".

mcqs.q: An invitation card can be made colourful with:
mcqs.why: An invitation card can be made colourful with drawings, and we should not forget to draw a picture on it.

lessons.title: 5.4 Grammar - Past Progressive Tense
lessons.notes_html:
Was and Were with -ing

The past progressive tense uses was or were with a verb ending in -ing. It tells about actions that were going on in the past. We use was with one person and were with more than one.

Examples

  • When I phoned my friends, they were playing monopoly.
  • Yesterday at six I was preparing dinner.
  • The kids were playing in the garden.
  • I was practising for the qirat competition when you came home.
  • While Danial was working in his room, his friends were swimming in the pool.
  • Most of the time we were sitting in the park.

Marvi and Rano's Day

Rano was cleaning the house. Marvi was washing the clothes. Their mothers were cooking and working. The sisters were playing with the baby. In the evening they were watching television and were enjoying themselves.

Key Points

  • Past progressive = was/were + verb-ing.
  • Was is for one; were is for more than one.
  • It shows actions going on in the past.

mcqs.q: Yesterday at six I ___ dinner.
mcqs.why: "I" takes "was", and the past progressive is was + verb-ing: I was preparing dinner.

mcqs.q: The kids ___ in the garden.
mcqs.why: The kids are more than one, so we use "were": The kids were playing in the garden.

mcqs.q: While Danial ___ in his room, his friends were swimming.
mcqs.why: Danial is one person, so we use "was working". His friends take "were swimming".

mcqs.q: Most of the time we ___ in the park.
mcqs.why: "We" takes "were" in the past progressive: We were sitting in the park.

mcqs.q: The past progressive tense is made with:
mcqs.why: Past progressive uses "was" or "were" with a verb ending in "ing" for actions going on in the past.

mcqs.q: When I phoned my friends, they ___ monopoly.
mcqs.why: "They" takes "were": When I phoned my friends, they were playing monopoly.

mcqs.q: Rano: "I ___ the house yesterday."
mcqs.why: Rano is one person talking about yesterday, so: I was cleaning the house.

mcqs.q: Marvi's mother ___ in the fields.
mcqs.why: Mother is one person, so we use "was": My mother was working in the fields.

mcqs.q: Rano's sisters ___ with the baby.
mcqs.why: Sisters are more than one, so we use "were playing".

mcqs.q: "We were watching television in the evening" - this tense tells about:
options: Actions going on in the past
mcqs.why: The past progressive tells about actions that were going on at a time in the past.

lessons.title: 5.4 Grammar - Can and Can't
lessons.notes_html:
Can Shows Ability

Can shows ability - that we are able to do something. Can't (cannot) shows that we are not able to do it.

Sentences in the Right Order

  • I cannot speak Arabic.
  • Can you please tell me the time?
  • She can't dance but she can sing.
  • Can they swim 100 metres?

Jaweria Can and Can't

Jaweria can read books, play ludo, sing and feed the goats. She can't play carum board, write songs, swim or ride a horse.

The Magic Pen

Zoha's magic pen writes invisibly. "Can you write with it? Yes, I can. Can you see now? Yes, I can, but I can't understand how it works. When we put light on the writing it will glow and you can see it. Can I also try? Sure you can, but you can't keep it forever!"

Key Points

  • Can = able to; can't = not able to.
  • Questions with can begin with "Can" and a capital letter.
  • Sentences begin with a capital letter and end with a full stop or question mark.

mcqs.q: "Can" shows:
mcqs.why: "Can" shows ability and "can't" shows that we are not able to do something.

mcqs.q: Put in order: "Arabic cannot speak I"
mcqs.why: The correct order is: I cannot speak Arabic. Sentences begin with a capital letter and end with a full stop.

mcqs.q: "you me time can please tell the" - the correct sentence is:
options: Tell me the time can you please?
Can you please tell me the time?
You can tell me please the time?
Please time tell me can you?
mcqs.why: Questions with "can" begin with Can: Can you please tell me the time? It ends with a question mark.

mcqs.q: Which of these can Jaweria do?
mcqs.why: Jaweria says: I can read books and I can play ludo, but I can't play carum board or write songs.

mcqs.q: Which of these can't Jaweria do?
mcqs.why: Jaweria can't swim or ride a horse, but she can sing, feed the goats and play ludo.

mcqs.q: Abdullah: "___ you write with it?" Zoha: "Yes, I can."
mcqs.why: The magic pen dialogue begins: Can you write with it? Yes, I can.

mcqs.q: Abdullah can see the writing but he ___ understand how it works.
mcqs.why: Abdullah says: Yes, I can, but I can't understand how it works.

mcqs.q: How does the magic pen's writing become visible?
options: When we put light on the writing, it will glow
mcqs.why: Zoha says: When we put light on the writing it will glow and you can see it.

mcqs.q: "Sure you can, but you ___ keep it forever!"
mcqs.why: Zoha allows Abdullah to try the pen but says he can't keep it forever.

mcqs.q: Which sentence is correct?
options: I can play ludo, but I can't play carum board.
I can play ludo but i cant play carum board
I can't play ludo but I can carum board play.
mcqs.why: It begins with a capital letter, uses can and can't correctly, and ends with a full stop.

lessons.title: 5.4 Grammar - Will: Talking about the Future
lessons.notes_html:
Will + Verb

We use will with the verb to talk about the future.

  • They will buy a new house next year.
  • You will get a lot of money on Eid day.
  • My mother will cook my favourite dish tomorrow.
  • The teacher will take us to the park on Saturday.
  • The train will leave at 8 o'clock.

Saeed and the Palmist

Saeed, 18 years old, asked an old palmist about his future. The palmist said: You will be very happy. You will get a lot of money. You will buy a beautiful house. Your friends will be jealous of you. You will travel around the world. People will serve you. But all this will happen only when you are 70 years old!

My Future

Tomorrow I will go to school. Next week I will visit my grandmother. Next year I will be in class V. After 5 years I will be in class IX.

Key Points

  • Will is used with the verb for the future.
  • Tomorrow, next week and next year show future time.
  • The palmist's joke: Saeed must wait till he is 70.

mcqs.q: They ___ a new house next year.
mcqs.why: "Next year" shows the future, so we use will + verb: They will buy a new house.

mcqs.q: The train ___ at 8 o'clock.
mcqs.why: We use "will" with the verb to talk about the future: The train will leave at 8 o'clock.

mcqs.q: My mother ___ my favourite dish tomorrow.
mcqs.why: "Tomorrow" shows the future: My mother will cook my favourite dish tomorrow.

mcqs.q: We use "will" with the verb to talk about:
mcqs.why: We use "will" with the verb to talk about the future.

mcqs.q: Who did Saeed ask about his future?
mcqs.why: Saeed, 18 years old, asked an old palmist about his future.

mcqs.q: According to the palmist, Saeed will:
options: Get a lot of money and buy a beautiful house
mcqs.why: The palmist said Saeed will be happy, get a lot of money and buy a beautiful house.

mcqs.q: What is the joke in the palmist's words?
options: All this will happen only when Saeed is 70 years old
mcqs.why: The joke is that Saeed must wait until he is 70 years old for all these good things.

mcqs.q: "Your friends ___ jealous of you."
mcqs.why: The palmist talks about the future: Your friends will be jealous of you.

mcqs.q: "After 5 years, I ___ in class IX."
mcqs.why: "After 5 years" is future time, so we say: I will be in class IX.

mcqs.q: Which words show future time?
options: Tomorrow, next week and next year
mcqs.why: Tomorrow, next week, next month and next year are future time words used with "will".

lessons.title: 5.5 Study Skills - Poem: Good Deeds
lessons.notes_html:
The Poem

The poem "Good Deeds" is sung on the tune of "Row, row, row your boat". Singing with actions helps us remember the poem and its message.

"Help, help, help around, helping shows you care. Smile, smile, smile all day, a smile makes you the best. Plant, plant, plant more trees, grow them all around. Listen, listen, listen now, remember all these things."

What the Poem Teaches

  • Help others around - helping shows you care.
  • Smile all day.
  • Plant more trees.
  • Listen and obey.

Rhyming Words in the Poem

  • care - pair (more: share, fare, dare, air, fair, hair)
  • best - rest (more: test, nest, vest)
  • around - ground (more: found, round, sound, pound)
  • things - brings (more: kings, rings, sings, springs)

Rhyming words end with the same sound. Adding more words to each family builds our vocabulary.

Key Points

  • Good deeds: help, smile, plant trees, listen and obey.
  • The poem is sung on the tune of "Row, row, row your boat".
  • Care, best, around and things are rhyming families in the poem.

mcqs.q: The poem "Good Deeds" is sung on the tune of:
mcqs.why: The poem "Good Deeds" is sung on the tune of "Row, row, row your boat", with actions.

mcqs.q: What does the poem teach us to do?
options: Help others, smile, plant trees and listen
mcqs.why: The poem teaches good deeds: help others around, smile all day, plant more trees, and listen and obey.

mcqs.q: "Helping shows you ___" - complete the line.
mcqs.why: The poem says: Help, help, help around, helping shows you care.

mcqs.q: What makes you the best, according to the poem?
mcqs.why: The poem says: Smile, smile, smile all day, a smile makes you the best.

mcqs.q: What should we plant more of?
mcqs.why: The poem says: Plant, plant, plant more trees, grow them all around.

mcqs.q: Which word rhymes with "care" in the poem?
mcqs.why: Care rhymes with pair. Share, fare, dare, air, fair and hair also belong to this family.

mcqs.q: Which word rhymes with "best"?
mcqs.why: Best rhymes with rest. Test, nest and vest are more words in this family.

mcqs.q: Which word can be added to the family of "around - ground"?
mcqs.why: Sound rhymes with around and ground. Found, round and pound also belong to this family.

mcqs.q: Which word rhymes with "things"?
mcqs.why: Things rhymes with brings. Kings, rings, sings and springs are also in this family.

mcqs.q: Rhyming words are words that:
mcqs.why: Rhyming words end with the same sound, and adding more words to each family builds our vocabulary.

lessons.title: 5.6 Fun - Masoom Monkey's Mystery Question
lessons.notes_html:
The Mystery Question

Masoom Monkey has written a question in a secret code: "AEHV STP XVVO RS CEOEOE?" We decode it letter by letter using the tips: A=H, E=A, H=V, V=E, S=Y, T=O, P=U, X=S, O=N, R=M, C=B.

Decoding Step by Step

  • A=H, E=A, H=V, V=E gives HAVE
  • S=Y, T=O, P=U gives YOU
  • X=S, V=E, V=E, O=N gives SEEN
  • R=M, S=Y gives MY
  • C=B, E=A, O=N, E=A, O=N, E=A gives BANANA

So Masoom Monkey is asking: "HAVE YOU SEEN MY BANANA?" Decoding letter by letter is a fun way to practise the alphabet.

Key Points

  • Each code letter stands for another letter.
  • The decoded question is "Have you seen my banana?"
  • Decoding practises the alphabet.

mcqs.q: What is the decoded mystery question?
mcqs.why: Decoding letter by letter gives: HAVE YOU SEEN MY BANANA?

mcqs.q: In the code, the letter A stands for:
mcqs.why: The tips say: Change A's with H. So A stands for H.

mcqs.q: The first code word "AEHV" decodes to:
mcqs.why: A=H, E=A, H=V, V=E gives the word HAVE, letter by letter.

mcqs.q: The code word "STP" decodes to:
mcqs.why: S=Y, T=O, P=U gives the word YOU, the second word of the question.

mcqs.q: The code word "XVVO" decodes to:
mcqs.why: X=S, V=E, V=E, O=N gives the word SEEN, the third word of the question.

mcqs.q: The last code word "CEOEOE" decodes to:
mcqs.why: C=B, E=A, O=N, E=A, O=N, E=A gives the word BANANA.

mcqs.q: In the code, the letter R stands for:
mcqs.why: The tips say: Change R's with M. So RS decodes to MY.

mcqs.q: Who is asking the mystery question?
mcqs.why: It is Masoom Monkey's mystery question: Have you seen my banana?

mcqs.q: Decoding this question is a fun way to practise:
mcqs.why: Decoding letter by letter is a fun way to practise the alphabet.

mcqs.q: In the code, the letter C stands for:
mcqs.why: The tips say: Change C's with B. That is why CEOEOE begins with B: BANANA.

lessons.title: Extra Reading - Money is Not Everything
lessons.notes_html:
About Extra Reading

The Story: Money is Not Everything

Sajid Ali was poor and sad. A wise old man showed him that his hands and eyes are worth more than gold. The story teaches us that money is not everything: health, strength and hard work matter more than money.

The Poem: Safety First

The poem "Safety First" repeats the road-safety rules:

  • Look up and down the street.
  • Listen for a horn or bell.
  • Wait until the road is clear.
  • Then run across safely.

Key Points

  • Health, strength and hard work are worth more than money.
  • Our hands and eyes are worth more than gold.
  • Cross the road only when it is clear.
